title: CAS Formal Substrate Manifest
description: Version tracking and schema inventory for the CAS Formal Substrate (CAS-ADR-008). The manifest records which schemas are present in each version, their status, and their role within the substrate.

organization.description: The formal substrate is organized by component (SAGE, ROOT Harness) with domain-specific configuration files produced by domain instantiation documents. Each component directory contains configuration schemas (JSON Schema), API operation contracts (OpenAPI 3.1.0), and data model schemas (JSON Schema) as appropriate.

structure.sage/: SAGE configuration schemas, Core API OpenAPI specification, and data model schemas. vault_config.schema.json is the root configuration schema; it $ref's to the five sub-schemas.
structure.root_harness/: ROOT Harness configuration schemas, Orchestration API OpenAPI specification, event stream schema, and interrupt contracts.
structure.cas_app_api.openapi.yaml: CAS Application API OpenAPI specification (workflow tools mounted under /app prefix).

schemas.title: SAGE Vault Configuration
schemas.role: Root schema for SAGE vault configuration. A domain instantiation produces a single YAML file that validates against this schema.

schemas.title: SAGE Core API Configuration
schemas.role: Stack-wide configuration for the SAGE Core API process (CAS-ADR-030, CAS-ADR-042, CAS-ADR-043). Loaded once at process startup before any vault is registered; carries resources whose enforcement spans the whole SAGE process (the abstraction provider, its model, and the local provider's optional context-window override and clause (f) opener constraint), the deployment-profile marker that co-binds the adapter-port implementations for one deployment target, the durable-storage binding selector (postgres, the storage port's sole binding), the vault-source-store binding selector (filesystem default, tenant document-store alternative), the Postgres storage-engine connection parameters (non-secret; password from the environment), the optional OAuth resource-server auth binding (absent by default; non-secret issuer/audience coordinates when a deployment authenticates its callers), and the caller-local transfer channel block (the public endpoint base minted recipes embed and the one-time token lifetime; omitted by deployments that never mint recipes). The on-disk file is sage/config.yaml at the repo root.

schemas.title: SAGE Document Types
schemas.role: Defines the doc_type enum for a vault's domain vocabulary. Tier 2 (the vocabulary itself), optional Tier 3 metadata_schema (per-doc_type structured metadata schema for tier3_metadata payloads), and optional unique_keys declaration (tier3_metadata fields whose values must be unique within the doc_type, enforced atomically by the storage substrate per CAS-ADR-031).

schemas.title: SAGE Lifecycle State Machine
schemas.role: Defines lifecycle states and valid transitions. Base set is always present; domains extend it.

schemas.title: SAGE Metadata Extraction Configuration
schemas.role: Defines the two-stage metadata extraction pipeline: filename patterns with code-to-doc_type maps, then content extraction rules.

schemas.title: SAGE Edge Inference Configuration
schemas.role: Defines three-tier edge inference model: tier assignments, inference rules, and staging table behavior.

schemas.title: SAGE Edge Type Registry
schemas.role: Per-vault registry assigning a resolution_policy to every edge type used by the vault. Consulted at edge creation for write-time invariant enforcement and at traversal for chain-scoped resolution. See CAS-ADR-017.

schemas.title: SAGE Core API
schemas.role: OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the SAGE Core API. Defines the REST surface for discovery, ingestion, lifecycle management, graph operations, access control, utilities, and the token-gated transfer endpoints (the byte legs of the caller-local transfer channel), plus the transfer recipe schemas the MCP tools return. Consumed by the ROOT Harness Integration Layer, MCP adapter, and CAS Application. Source authority: SAGE Architecture Reference Section 7.

schemas.title: CAS Application API
schemas.role: OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the CAS Application backend HTTP surface (mounted at the /app prefix). Defines directory scan and batch-ingest endpoints used by the CAS Application UI. Architecturally distinct from the SAGE Core API; the two specs are validated together by tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py and must respect URL-prefix boundaries (sage_core_api owns /sage_vaults/*, cas_app_api owns /app/*).

schemas.title: Decision Log
schemas.role: Schema for SAGE-managed decision logs owned by steward and orchestrator agents. Captures operational judgment not recorded in artifact revision histories: decisions not to act, decisions deferred, and cross-artifact reasoning. Append-only with supersession back-references. See CAS-ADR-012.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Pipeline Configuration
schemas.role: Defines pipeline stages, transitions, gatekeeper bindings, and precondition expressions.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Agent Registration
schemas.role: Defines agent registration records: type, owned artifact, autonomy level, capabilities, policy reference, LLM configuration.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Policy Configuration
schemas.role: Defines behavioral constraints: permitted operations, scope restrictions, and tool-level approval policy.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Workflow Graph
schemas.role: Defines LangGraph workflow definitions: nodes, edges, state dictionary, and interrupt placement.

schemas.title: ROOT Harness Orchestration API
schemas.role: OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification for the ROOT Harness Orchestration API. Defines the REST surface for workflow triggering, status monitoring, human-in-the-loop interrupt resolution, agent registration, pipeline status queries, and real-time event streaming. Consumed by the CAS Application, MCP adapter, and CLI. Source authority: ROOT Harness Architecture Reference Section 2.5.

schemas.title: AgentEvent
schemas.role: Schema for typed event records emitted by the ROOT Harness event stream during workflow execution. Seven event categories: workflow lifecycle, node transitions, tool interactions, LLM cycles, interrupt lifecycle, steward governance, and checkpoint operations. Consumed by the CAS Application and MCP clients via subscribe_events. See CAS-ADR-013.

schemas.title: Interrupt Contracts
schemas.role: Schema for human-in-the-loop interrupt descriptors and tool-level approval policies. Defines InterruptDescriptor (runtime data structure for pending interrupts), ApproveRequest (resolution payload for the approve operation), and ApprovalPolicy (per-agent configuration for tool-call approval gating). Two interrupt origins: interrupt nodes (autonomy Level 3) and approval callbacks (Levels 1-2). See ROOT Harness Architecture Reference Sections 2.5, 2.7, 4.4, and 5.2.

revision_history.summary: Correct the identifier_mention prose to the resolver that exists (edge_inference.schema.json 0.3 -> 0.4). Three descriptions described behavior the engine had moved on from. The inference-method enum said identifier_mention resolves via tag and title-prefix lookups; title matching was removed when identifier resolution moved to tier3_metadata, and the configuration loader has warned about the leftover target_title_prefix key ever since -- so the schema advertised as a resolution path the very thing the loader reports as inert. That key was itself still described as a live filter applied after tag/tier3 filtering, and now states that it is retired, ignored by the resolver, accepted only so a pre-migration configuration keeps loading, and surfaced as a load warning -- with the reason a pattern leaning on it resolves nothing useful: its remaining filters are a generic tag matching every document of the type. And both placeholder-bearing fields documented {id} alone, where the substitution helper has always also supplied {adr_num}, the matched literal trailing digit run, which is what a vault whose stored identifier drops a prefix the mention carries must use -- as the canonical vault ADR pattern does. target_tags and target_tier3 now name both placeholders and say what each substitutes. target_tier3 additionally records the consequence of choosing between them: a value of exactly {id} makes the pattern reach over the target doc_type declared identifier space measurable at config load, where a derived placeholder is not invertible and is left unmeasured. That is the boundary of the new identifier_mention_id_space_warnings pass in sage/config.py, stated where a configuration author chooses between the two rather than only in the code that enforces it. Description text only: no property, type, constraint, or required-key change, and nothing mirrored into a Pydantic model, since edge_inference is carried as a passed-through dict rather than a modeled section.

Disclose that catalog ordering is total (sage_core_api.openapi.yaml 0.34 -> 0.35). Every ORDER BY the catalog document query could produce left ties -- the default on lifecycle then document_date, a supplied sort_by on that one column, and the fallback on title alone -- and Postgres may return tied rows in any order, and need not choose the same one twice. Two things depended on it doing so: limit/offset paging, which can skip a row or return it twice when the two queries disagree about where the page boundary falls, and the catalog budget hint, whose recommended_limit is measured by truncating the response already in hand on the premise that a lower limit returns the same rows truncated. The edge enumeration arm carried the same defect, ordering by created_at alone. Two substrate-visible description changes, both on field descriptions rather than the operation description, and both mirrored byte-identically into the Pydantic models per the description-parity gate: DiscoverRequest.sort_by gains 'Ties are broken by document id, so the order is total and paging a filtered set returns each document exactly once.'; DiscoverResponse.results gains 'Both orderings are total -- ties broken by document id for documents, by edge id for edges -- so paging returns each row exactly once.' No parameter, schema, or error-code change; no wire-protocol break. Implementation in sage/storage/postgres/graph_store.py: a new module constant _ORDER_TIEBREAK (', id ASC') is appended by _build_order_clause, restructured so every branch contributes only its primary sort expression and all of them return through one exit -- a branch added later cannot be total-by-oversight, which is how all three came to admit ties; query_edges gains ', e.id ASC' and a docstring stating the same requirement. Premises stated where they are relied on: _response_at_row_count and _facets_response_at_cap in sage/services/retrieval.py (the facets order was already total -- values come from a GROUP BY on the field, so value ASC has no tie left to break -- and is unchanged), and the query_documents port docstring in sage/adapters/interfaces.py. The search MCP tool's sort_by Args entry carries the same sentence. Tests: tests/sage/test_graph_store.py adds a parametrized clause-totality gate derived from _SORTABLE_COLUMNS plus paging, order-stability, and edge-paging tests over fixtures that tie on every sortable column and whose scan order is perturbed between calls; tests/sage/test_retrieval.py adds a re-page test asserting the delivered byte count and the prefix identity, and a facets test pinning that arm's order as already total.

Make the facets response size guarantee byte-aware (sage_core_api.openapi.yaml 0.33 -> 0.34). The facets target of search bounds each row's value map by count -- a per-field cap, 50 by default -- which makes the response independent of corpus size and tagging density but only in the unit it counts. The failure the cap was built against was denominated in bytes: a facets response exceeding the calling client's tool-result ceiling. Fifty tag strings of a thousand characters clear the cap completely, truncating nothing, and still overrun the 24 KiB inline budget, and the facets dispatch deliberately emitted no budget hint, so nothing downstream measured the payload. The count bound is unchanged; this adds the byte-denominated companion beside it. New _apply_facets_budget_hint in sage/services/retrieval.py, applied by the dispatcher after the vocabulary warnings, merges reason="facets_response_exceeds_inline_budget", response_size_bytes, budget_bytes, and recommended_facet_value_limit into hints when the serialized response exceeds the budget. Separate from the catalog hint rather than shared with it, on both keys: the catalog hint's recommended_limit names limit, which this target rejects via mode_parameter_mismatch, so a shared hint would recommend a re-call the validator refuses; and a distinct reason keeps a consumer switching on response_exceeds_inline_budget from being handed a payload whose recommended_limit is silently absent. The recommendation is measured rather than modelled: a binary search over the cap, simulating each candidate re-call by truncating every row to it and serializing, returns the largest cap that fits. The catalog hint's proportional model does not transfer to this target and the independent review of this branch showed why. It treats the response's fixed part -- the envelope, and every vocabulary row already shorter than the cap -- as though it shrank with the cap, so the re-call lands above budget by that fixed part times the fraction the response was over; measured at a 3.6 KB envelope the re-call missed by 226 bytes and the hint fired again. And it scales the widest row, which need not be the heaviest: a wide row of short vocabulary values beside a narrow row of long tags puts the bytes and the entry count in different rows, and only the entry count is what the model reads -- measured, that walked 50 -> 22 -> 16 -> 12 -> 9 with three over-budget re-calls where one would do. Simulation has neither problem and the payload carries at most one row per facet field, so a logarithmic number of serializations costs nothing worth modelling around. The recommendation is omitted when no cap below the one in force fits, so the hint never names a re-call that would not help. Pass 2 of the review found the measurement itself denominated in the wrong encoding: the shared helper claimed to report the bytes the MCP runtime delivers and reported a compact json.dumps, where the runtime encodes the dict the tool layer returns with pydantic_core.to_json(..., indent=2). Indentation costs bytes per element rather than per byte of content, so the delta grows with value count -- about 1% on fifty thousand-character tags and 17% on the high-cardinality short-value vocabularies the per-field count cap exists for, which is to say a compact measurement understates the delivered size most in exactly the shape the hint is for. A margin-free search fitted to that number therefore named re-calls that overrun the delivered ceiling. The helper now reproduces both halves of the delivered encoding. Correcting it exposed the same over-recommendation in the pre-existing catalog hint, whose re-page test had compared two compact measurements against each other and so was self-consistent rather than correct, so the search generalizes into a shared _largest_fitting_prefix over a caller-supplied truncation and both hints now use it. The catalog hint keeps recommended_limit unconditionally present, falling back to 1 where nothing fits, because callers have been able to rely on that key since it shipped; the facets hint omits it, being new. Advisory only: nothing is truncated, facet_value_limit and total_distinct semantics are untouched, and an adaptive cap was rejected precisely because it would make an explicit facet_value_limit=50 return fewer than 50 values as a function of measured bytes. Shared _serialized_response_bytes extracted so both hints measure the same encoding the MCP runtime delivers. Substrate: the RetrievalTarget, FacetHit, DiscoverRequest.facet_value_limit and DiscoverResponse.hints descriptions now say which bound is denominated in values and which in bytes, and the discover operation description gains the same statement the search tool docstring makes, so the docstring/spec disclosure pin holds at its measured (3, 11) rather than widening. New coverage: a production-budget regression on fifty thousand-character tags whose in-test arithmetic guard proves the overrun is structural, asserting fifty-of-fifty values with total_distinct equal to it so the count bound is visibly satisfied while the byte-aware element fires; a narrow-tag control at identical document count, value count and total_distinct that must not fire, discriminating bytes from cardinality; a re-call at the recommendation that must clear the hint, with the recommendation asserted strictly above the floor so an implementation collapsing every recommendation to 1 reddens; synthetic-payload tests that hold the envelope and the widest-versus-heaviest row shape at values a real vault cannot reach, each asserting both that the simulated re-call fits and that the proportional value would not, so the fixture carries the discriminating arithmetic rather than a magic number; the degenerate cap-of-one case that omits the recommendation; an under-budget negative control; an MCP-wrapper test, since the boundary the original failure crossed is one a service-level assertion never reaches; and a delivered-bytes assertion driven through FastMCP's own call_tool on a six-hundred-value short-tag vocabulary, which is the assertion this guarantee is actually about and the only one denominated in the units the ceiling is. That fixture shape is load-bearing: the same test on the wide-tag shape passes against the compact encoding, because there the two differ by 1% (tests/sage/test_retrieval.py, tests/app/test_mcp_app_tools.py). The test that pinned the deliberate skip is rewritten rather than deleted: its assertion that no recommended_limit appears survives as the guard that the facets hint never names the parameter this target rejects.

Preserve the request validator's own message when a mode_parameter_mismatch rejection crosses the request boundary. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.32->v0.33: the discover operation's 400 response description, previously naming only "unknown mode, scope, or filter field", now names mode_parameter_mismatch and its detail shape -- the spec's only mechanism for settling an error code's detail, since ErrorResponse is one generic envelope whose detail is additionalProperties and carries no per-code schema. DiscoverRequest._reject_mode_parameter_mismatch enforces ten constraints, three on the mode axis and seven on the target axis, and writes each rejection a message in the terms it actually enforces. Because sage.models cannot import sage.api under the models-are-a-leaf-layer contract, the rejection crossed the boundary as a PydanticCustomError carrying only {mode, forbidden_param, allowed_modes}, and the translator in sage/api/errors.py rebuilt ModeParameterMismatchError from those three fields alone -- discarding the message and composing a sentence about mode. Every target-constrained branch therefore reached the caller naming the wrong axis, self-contradictorily so wherever the branch set allowed_modes=[catalog]: search(mode=catalog, target=documents, facet_fields=[tags]) was refused with "Parameter 'facet_fields' is not valid for mode 'catalog'. Allowed modes for 'facet_fields': ['catalog']", which refuses the mode it simultaneously reports as allowed and never names target, the parameter the caller has to change. Three changes at the translation seam. (1) ModeParameterMismatchError.__init__ takes (message, detail) instead of (mode, forbidden_param, allowed_modes): it is now a typed envelope over the validator's message rather than a second account of the rejection, sorting whichever allowed-set key is present so ordering is a property of the envelope rather than of the order a branch listed its members in. (2) The translator passes err["msg"] through -- Pydantic has already rendered the template with the ctx placeholders substituted, so carrying it across reads what is there rather than widening ctx -- and filters ctx through the new module-scope _MODE_MISMATCH_DETAIL_KEYS whitelist, which keeps a branch's own message-template context (key, on the filter-key branches) out of the published envelope by default. (3) Each of the ten branches now reports both axes' current values and the allowed set for the one it constrains: allowed_modes where the parameter needs a different mode, allowed_targets where it needs a different target, never both, since naming a set on the unconstrained axis describes a change that does not lift the rejection. The allowed-target sets are derived from the sibling branches rather than asserted: the edges-target branch is what makes seven of the facets-target parameters documents-only, while response_mode, limit and offset are absent from it and so remain open to edges; the two sets are named once as _DOCUMENTS_ONLY and _DOCUMENTS_AND_EDGES beside the filter-key tuples. The leaf-layer contract is untouched. New coverage at tests/sage/test_retrieval.py: a sixteen-row case table over all ten branches, asserting the delivered message equals the validator's own rendering read back on the same run rather than a second copy of the string, that detail names exactly the constrained axis and excludes key, and -- the anti-coincidental trap -- that the delivered message is not a composition of the detail actually delivered, plus a source-counted guard that the table covers every rejection site. tests/sage/test_validation_envelope_parity.py gains the code's first two-surface coverage and the first HTTP-surface assertion of this envelope at all, on one mode-constrained and one target-constrained rejection, with an independent content pin because parity alone passes vacuously when both surfaces regress together. Co-shipped caller-facing change surfaced by the same branch survey: the query parameter is now refused outside the two scoring modes rather than only in deterministic mode. Nothing consumed it elsewhere -- request.query is read by _keyword, _semantic and their boost and warning helpers, and by none of _catalog, _catalog_facets or _catalog_edges -- so search(mode=catalog, query=...) was accepted, the query dropped, and the whole filtered set returned with nothing in the response to say it had not been searched: the silent-ignore failure the validator's own facet and edge branches exist to prevent. Stated once by widening the existing branch's condition to "not a scoring mode" rather than by adding a near-duplicate catalog branch, which makes its allowed_modes=[semantic, keyword] true by construction instead of by coincidence; the message template takes {mode} in place of the hardcoded 'deterministic'. Mode-axis checks already run ahead of target-axis ones -- heading_path has behaved this way since the edges target landed -- so a catalog-plus-edges call carrying a query reports the mode axis, consistently with its heading_path sibling. The catalog-mode description on both the tool docstring and the operation narrative now says a query is refused rather than that none is needed.

Serve the default vault-config scaffold instead of restating it per caller. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.31->v0.32: one new operation, get_default_vault_config on GET /sage_vaults/default-config, taking the prospective vault id as a required query parameter and returning the creation-time scaffold as an untyped config object -- the same inline {type: object, additionalProperties: true} schema the per-vault config read already returns, so no components/schemas entry and no Pydantic counterpart. The scaffold had two copies. VaultRegistryService.get_default_config built one; the CAS Application's create-vault form restated the whole of it -- doc types, lifecycle states and transitions, edge inference, abstraction toggle -- as a TypeScript literal and posted that. They drifted: when the Python scaffold gained completed --supersede--> archived and completed --reactivate--> active, the client kept the old six-row table, so a vault created through the UI inherited exactly the gap that change closed. A second divergence was live and unnoticed: the client wrote storage_root as a tilde string where the scaffold writes the expanded absolute path the identity schema documents. Both end here. The operation is deliberately not vault-scoped and is pinned as such in SAGE_NON_VAULT_PATHS: the scaffold precedes the vault, so a {vault_id} segment would promise a registry resolution the route must not perform -- an unregistered id is served, not 404'd. It sits under /sage_vaults/ all the same, because the CAS Application reaches SAGE through a backend-for-frontend that proxies that subtree and nothing else. It is REST-only, allowlisted in HTTP_ONLY_OPERATIONS: the operation exists so a browser client can read a scaffold it cannot construct, and an in-process caller reaches the same builder directly. Two narrative pins drain against that one addition. The create_vault prose on both surfaces named VaultRegistryService.get_default_config as the only affordance for a default config, justified in UNRESOLVED_IDENTIFIERS by no API route returning one; the prose now names the operation, whose id is in the contract vocabulary, and the two pins come out. Code (not in this substrate): get_default_config's name and owner parameters default to empty strings, the two identity fields the server cannot know, which the caller fills before posting; the web client fetches the scaffold on submit rather than on panel open, the vault id being still in flight until then. Tests: five REST cases in test_vault_config_api.py compare the served document against the builder rather than a transcribed config and hold the round trip to creating a vault verbatim, recorded as TEST-SAGE-VM-REST-004; three component cases pin that the client posts what it was served, built in the test from the served object, so a reintroduced literal fails on the comparison rather than on a restated expectation.

State the keyword match unit on the caller-facing surfaces. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.30->v0.31: two description edits, no schema, operation, or response-shape change. The discover operation's keyword-mode bullet and the RetrievalMode enum description both now say a document matches when it carries every term -- not necessarily together in one passage -- that the document is ranked by its best-matching passage, which is the excerpt returned, and that a quoted phrase is the exception and must be satisfied within a single passage (CAS-ADR-048). The enum description previously carried no conjunction clause at all and was the stalest of the four copies; it is not gated against the Python RetrievalMode docstring, since RetrievalMode sits in YAML_ONLY_FORWARD_DECLARATIONS in test_openapi_conformance.py, so the two were reconciled by hand. The MCP search docstring in sage/sage_api_tools.py is reworded to the same claims in the same change: test_mcp_docstring_disclosure_parity.py asserts the (3, 11) spec-only / doc-only divergence for the pair as an equality, so rewording one surface alone reddens it. Behaviour behind the prose changes with the PostgresContentStore keyword binding, which now resolves each top-level query operand to document ids and intersects them, leaving phrase adjacency chunk-scoped and barring the synthetic document-header row from the match union per CAS-ADR-049.

Declare the vault-source store's refusal on every path that reads or writes source bytes. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.29->v0.30: verify_vault_source_files, get_document, get_document_content, get_document_download_url and transfer_download each gain 502 and 503 responses, byte-identical to the two operations that already carried them and all $ref'ing the existing ErrorResponse; no schema, no operation shape change, no new component. The previous revision to declare these codes typed the refusal on the source-file repair and the ingest retention and left two paths untyped: the source-file audit, which reaches the store through the same observation helper the repair uses, so one store call answered a caller two different ways depending on which operation reached it; and the delivery-side reads, where a refusal surfaced as a bare 500 against a spec declaring only the request-shape and record-state refusals. The audit's behaviour under a refusal was the decision this revision exists to make, and it aborts: the walk ends, the typed error names the document the store declined on, and the findings already collected are discarded. The alternative -- a per-document integrity status alongside missing, hash_mismatch, symlinked and out_of_root -- would keep those findings, and was rejected on three grounds. It widens a published enumeration and its summary counts to describe a condition of the store rather than of the retained copy, which is what the other four values report; it needs a rule for what the counts mean when the store answered for some documents and not others, where the healthy count is a residual and so would silently absorb any document the walk could not classify; and it would perpetuate the divergence this change exists to close, the repair answering with a status code while the audit answered with a report. The audit is read-only and idempotent, so re-running it is the whole remedy for a refusal the binding called transient -- which is the case the 503 names. The enumeration is therefore unchanged at four values and the summary at five keys, and a test pins that so an implementation cannot type the refusal and widen the contract anyway. Of the delivery paths, the raw byte channel is typed only for the reads it resolves before returning: it hands back a chunk iterator the response pulls after the headers are out, so a refusal raised on that pull cannot become a status code, and the operation description is unchanged on that point rather than widened past what it can promise. The projection path was examined and carries nothing to declare -- it reads reconstructed chunks from the content store and never reaches the vault-source store, which an existing profile-invariance test already pins. The transfer channel's download leg is typed too, having been the third caller-facing surface reading a retained source and the last one left untyped; its token is the sole credential on that route, so an untyped failure cost the caller a spent token and told them nothing about whether re-issuing the originating call was worth doing, which is exactly what the two statuses distinguish. No counterpart to the upload leg's token-return is added there: that mechanism protects bytes the caller already paid to send, where a download token is re-minted for free and the source leg spools nothing, and the operation description already answers the question by saying a failed fetch is retried by re-issuing the originating call. Two operation descriptions are corrected rather than widened. get_document_content and the download leg both claimed every failure mode resolved before the stream opened, so errors always arrived as a structured envelope and never as a truncated body. That was already untrue -- both hand the response a chunk iterator first pulled after the headers are out -- and declaring a store-refusal status on those operations would have made a caller read it as a promise that a refusal always arrives as 502. They now separate the reads resolved before the stream opens from a refusal raised once bytes are flowing, and name the promised Content-Length as what tells a caller the delivery was cut short. The batch surfaces continue to declare neither code, for the reason recorded in v1.71. The re-projection read-back is swept with them. It reads the retained source back through the store from three callers -- the ingest pipeline's projection stage, the operator-facing recompute, and the worker's re-projection -- and the translation is placed at the read rather than at any caller, because only the innermost placement types it for all three. The ingest operation already declared both statuses and now actually returns them there; the recompute is an MCP tool with no HTTP operation, so it gains the codes in its own error-mode catalogue and nothing in this spec. The worker's path answers no caller at all. The store binding's *config* half -- the vault-config read, write, delete and discovery calls reaching the same client from create_vault, update_vault_config and vault teardown -- can raise the same refusal and is deliberately not swept here. It is a different surface with its own answer to make: those operations are the ones that decide whether a vault exists at all, so what a refusal means for a half-written config, and whether the teardown path should report or absorb one, is not settled by the read-path reasoning above. Recorded so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight. The two statuses' prose now differs between the read and write paths rather than being one string everywhere. The shared wording named an upload session in both halves -- a reply opening none, and one the store expired -- which on a read is a description of machinery the operation does not have; the five read paths drop those clauses and the two write paths keep them, where an upload session is a real thing that can fail. Code (not in this substrate): the audit wraps each document's observation in the existing service-boundary translation rather than the walk, so the error carries a source_path the caller can act on; the delivery regions wrap the whole store-touching block rather than the three read methods named, the write-to-path wrap sitting outside the cleanup that removes a partial target so a refused stream still leaves the caller's retry path clear. Tests: a new declaration-coverage gate asserts the set of operations declaring both statuses is exactly the set whose service path can raise them, pinned as an equality because the existing envelope gate is driven from the spec and so cannot see an operation that emits a status it never declared. Its expectation is derived from the code rather than listed: a walk over every module finds each function whose body opens the translation, a mapping from those sites to the operations that can surface them is asserted total in both directions, and the expected set is computed from it. A hand-kept roster would not have closed the gap it names -- the developer who adds a wrap and forgets the declaration forgets the roster in the same motion -- whereas an unmapped site fails by name. The walk reads one spelling: a bare-name call. A translation opened through a module-local wrapper, or written attribute-style or under an import alias, is invisible to it, and the ingest service is exactly where a wrapper is the idiom. Extending the walk to chase those spellings was considered and declined. The gate exists only because the translation is placed by hand at each call site, and the placement itself is what the two review passes on this change kept finding wrong -- first a site missed, then the gate guarding against missed sites blind to the module's own spelling. The intended answer is a translating wrapper around the store binding, applied where the binding is resolved, which covers every source-byte call by construction and makes this gate unnecessary rather than smarter; scoping it to the source-byte methods is what keeps the config half deliberately untyped, and the ingest retention keeps a wrap of its own so a refused retention still names the path as the caller spelled it. Teaching the walk a second spelling in the meantime would be building more of the thing being removed. The limit is therefore recorded in the gate's own docstrings rather than papered over. Two error-detail pins were added for the store_status key the new prose names, the contract typing detail as free-form; no other allowlist entries in any conformance or coverage gate.

Settle abstraction work a stopped worker drops, and name the status it settles at. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.28->v0.29. PipelineStatus gains a seventh member, abstraction_interrupted, taking the enum to projection_complete / indexing_in_progress / indexing_complete / abstraction_in_progress / abstraction_complete / abstraction_skipped / abstraction_interrupted / failed. The precipitating defect: reabstract stamps abstraction_in_progress durably before enqueueing an in-memory job, and stopping the drain worker cancels the job in flight and abandons every job still queued, neither of which stamps a terminal status -- so the document was left non-terminal with nothing running to advance it. Recovery was narrower than the code read: recover_incomplete_documents runs from the FastAPI lifespan only, so of the five worker-stop sites one was covered and the rest stranded until the next process start. The guarantee is placed inside stop_worker rather than at each site, because only the reload/hot-swap has a successor services object to recover onto -- eviction and the short-lived cloud sweep have none, so a per-site design writes the same re-stamp three times and still leaves a sixth site added later uncovered. delete_vault is the one documented opt-out (stop_worker(restamp=False)): the schema holding those documents is dropped moments later, so the record would be written to a store about to cease to exist. abstraction_interrupted joins TERMINAL_PIPELINE_STATUSES but not SUCCESSFUL_TERMINAL_PIPELINE_STATUSES, so pipeline_error survives to name the cause; terminal because nothing is left running, and unlike failed it records only that work was dropped, so recover_incomplete_documents re-enqueues it where it leaves skip and failure as operator territory. Reusing failed was rejected for exactly that: recovery deliberately leaves failed alone, so a graceful restart would have stopped auto-recovering interrupted work, and a benign self-inflicted interruption would have been indistinguishable from a provider fault. Two operation descriptions widen the terminal set they enumerate (reabstract_document, recompute_deferred_vault_abstracts), and the latter's recovery-contract paragraph is corrected: it named a stopped worker as the reachable cause of a document stranded at abstraction_in_progress, which is no longer one, leaving a slow generation as the case the wait ceiling exists for. The deferred sweep's own enumeration is deliberately NOT widened to the new status, while the out-of-band bulk sweep's default selector does gain it. Both dispatch through reabstract, which requires stored chunks and refuses a document without them, so chunk availability does not distinguish the two -- the caller does. The bulk sweep is an attended operator tool whose contract is to report what happened to each document in a worklist the operator selected and reads, where a refusal is a finding; the deferred sweep is an unattended contract an automated caller acts on, where the same refusal is noise. An earlier statement of this ground named chunk availability; it did not discriminate the two sweeps, both dispatching the same way, and is superseded by the caller distinction above. Code (not in this substrate): stop_worker snapshots the in-flight claims before cancelling (an interrupted job releases its own claim while unwinding, so a claim read afterwards no longer names it), drains the abandoned queue releasing each dropped job's claim -- a leak that outlived the work it guarded and rejected the next operation on that document as already in flight -- and stamps only documents still non-terminal, the check and the write sharing one hold of the document lock so a document that settled on its own is not overwritten with an interruption. Stamping is best-effort and logged: every caller runs it immediately before releasing the storage handle, so an error escaping would leak the pool it was about to close. Also in this revision, from the same disposition: HealthIndicators gains a fourth counter, interrupted_abstract_count, because the status this change introduces was reachable by the bulk sweep and by startup recovery but visible on no health surface -- a vault holding forty interrupted documents reported failed=0, deferred=0. It is counted apart from failed_ingestion_count rather than folded into it: no stage failed, and conflating the two would reintroduce on the health surface exactly the ambiguity this change rejected when it declined to reuse `failed` as the status. The CAS Application gains the matching card and a drill-down label. The Document.pipeline_error description widens on both surfaces, having described only the `failed` case while the field is now populated for the interrupted one too. The stop_worker docstring drops an inaccurate claim -- that every dropped document is released from its claim by the stop -- and names the window it over-approximates: reabstract and recompute_pipeline hold a claim across awaits before enqueueing, so a stop landing there stamps a document whose owner is still live and about to advance it, which costs a transient status rather than a lost outcome. ReabstractOutcome gains a sixth member, interrupted, taking the enum to success / skipped_pdf / llm_failure / still_skipped / timeout / interrupted, with a named arm before the residual fallthrough in both the service sweep and the out-of-band bulk sweep. Without it the settle path reported a document the worker had dropped as llm_failure -- the residual arm claims the provider raised, and its docstring invariant that only a stored `failed` reaches it had quietly become false. That is the same conflation this revision rejected when it declined to reuse `failed` as the pipeline status, arriving one surface later: the status distinguished the case and the outcome vocabulary then folded it back together. The widening carries the TypeScript union and REABSTRACT_FAILURE_OUTCOMES with it, the SSE status vocabulary being unchanged so a client switching on status alone keeps working. No schema or operation shape changes, no migration (pipeline_status is an unconstrained text column), and no allowlist entries in any conformance or coverage gate.

Declare what the vault-source store's refusal returns, on both operations that can raise it. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.27->v0.28: restore_vault_source_file and ingest_document each gain 502 and 503 responses, byte-identical between the two and both $ref'ing the existing ErrorResponse; no schema, no operation shape change, no new component. Both operations already declared the refusals decided from the request and the record before the store is touched, and neither declared the store itself declining the write it is handed -- which the spec's silence described as a server fault. The two statuses split those refusals the way a caller acts on them: 502 `vault_source_store_refused` where repeating cannot help (quota, a withdrawn permission, a reply that opens no usable upload session), 503 `vault_source_store_unavailable` where waiting is the whole remedy (throttling past the binding's one retry, a transient backend signal, an expired upload session). 5xx rather than 4xx because the request that reached SAGE was well formed and the fault is upstream; `detail.store_status` carries the status the store declined with. The batch operations are deliberately given neither: a per-file failure is collected into their success summary as a BatchIngestFileError carrying the error's code, so no batch surface can emit either status and declaring one it never returns would be its own divergence. That entry's own code vocabulary is enumerated nowhere and is tracked separately; it predates this change. Code (not in this substrate): the store binding raises a typed refusal carrying that classification instead of an untyped error, one translation at the service boundary turns it into these two codes while keeping the store's own response body in the log rather than on the wire, and the caller-local delivery gate returns a redeemed transfer token when the work it was redeemed for fails, so a refused write costs no second upload.

Bump the minor version to v2.2. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.26->v0.27 and cas_app_api.openapi.yaml v0.5->v0.6. The minor version had not moved since v2.1.0, 153 commits back, across the body of work that followed from discovering that the document store rewrites Office packages at rest; the bump was intended to land earlier in that work and was missed. The version is VCS-derived and single-sourced: sage/build_info.py resolves RELEASE_VERSION from `git describe --long --tags --match v*` and exposes API_VERSION as its MAJOR.MINOR contract segment, which both FastAPI applications read (sage/app.py, app/backend/asgi.py). Only the two committed specs carry a hand-edited literal, so the bump is a coordinated change rather than a single edit: the annotated tag v2.2.0 anchored on main, plus info.version "2.1" -> "2.2" in both specs. Sequencing is tag-first rather than tag-the-merge-commit. CI answers pull_request with a full-history, tag-bearing checkout, so a spec-edit branch authored before the tag exists reads API_VERSION 2.1 against specs declaring 2.2 and cannot go green; tagging first inverts the divergence onto main instead, where no workflow observes it, since no trigger fires on a tag push and the next push to main is the merge that closes the window. The gate of record is tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py::test_openapi_info_version_matches_api_version, the three-way check across the live /openapi.json and both committed specs. Its per-spec loop was verified by mutation in both arms: each spec reverted alone reddens the gate and names itself, so changing one and not the other fails exactly as changing neither does. A third probe confirmed the live document moved with the constants rather than the two file literals merely agreeing with each other. No schema, route, argument, or model shape changes, and no allowlist entries in any conformance or coverage gate. Downstream of the tag: container images bake SAGE_BUILD_VERSION 2.2.x via the Dockerfile build arg, the health endpoint reports it, and the MCP handshake advertises 2.2.x with the build identity.

Ground caller-facing prose in the contract it draws on. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.25->v0.26 and cas_app_api.openapi.yaml v0.4->v0.5. The precipitating defect is the class the previous revision fixed one instance of: both narratives of `chain` named a response field `linearity` and called it three-valued, where the model and the schema declare the boolean `is_linear`, so a caller read None and concluded a linear chain was non-linear with no error anywhere. Nothing gated it. The argument-conformance gate compares parameter shape, the description-parity gate compares Pydantic field descriptions against YAML property descriptions, and the docstring-disclosure gate compares the two prose surfaces to each other -- that last one makes the surfaces agree without asking whether what they agree on is true, and its module docstring records the boundary deliberately. Schema-axis findings, all corrected here. Eight $ref sites pointed at `#/components/schemas/VaultId` and `#/components/schemas/DocumentId`, which the spec never defined -- only the like-named `components/parameters` entries existed -- so the contract did not resolve for any consumer that followed them, this sweep's own vocabulary walk included; both schemas are now declared as the constrained scalars they are, and carried in Python as the existing validating type aliases rather than as models, which is why they are forward-declared YAML-only. Eight fields were declared by a response model and by no YAML property, so the API returned them and the published contract never mentioned them: Document.metadata_confirmed (which four caller-facing narratives name), DocumentSummary.{document_date, source_modified_at, source_path} (which DocumentSummaryLight's own description already listed as fields it omits from DocumentSummary), BulkLifecycleItemResult.created_edge, ChainResponse.{total_length, available_edge_types}, and the CAS App ErrorResponse.read_meta. The forward-direction coverage test could not see any of them: it asserts YAML properties are a subset of the model's fields, which is silent on the mirror case, and the verbatim description-parity gate iterates YAML properties, so a property that does not exist has no description to compare. Implementation-axis findings, bounded to the fifteen operations whose descriptions make a falsifiable cost or vocabulary assertion and all landing on `chain`. Its cost claim covered the walk's two statements and omitted both the existence check preceding them and the two further edge queries a one-document chain makes to fill available_edge_types -- three round-trips for a chain of two or more, four for a chain of one, which spends the hint's two queries but skips the edge query because the storage walk returns early when the CTE yields a single row, against a sentence that read as two. `length` was documented as the chain total on both prose surfaces and in both schemas where the service assigns it after slicing, so a caller paging with `limit` read the page size as the total, the same silent-wrong-value shape as `linearity`; it now says what it counts and total_length carries the total. And the chain array claimed its head sits at position length-1, where positions are assigned over the full ordered chain before slicing and a page taken at an offset keeps them absolute. One further cost claim was stale rather than wrong when written: recompute_deferred_vault_abstracts anchored its per-document wall-clock to a model the committed configuration no longer names, and now says a local MLX model, which config chooses and prose need not track. The enumerations the pass read are sound: StalenessBasis does carry the four buckets verify_vault_drift claims, the four integrity_status values verify_vault_source_files names are the four the schema declares, and the three terminal statuses recompute_deferred_vault_abstracts says it polls for are exactly the set its poller waits on -- read against the widened set and bounded wait that landed in 1.68, which moved prose and poller together. Seven operations named internal implementation identifiers in prose whose readers cannot reach them; five had them reworded as telling the caller nothing -- nine identifiers, one of them on two of those operations (a service class path, a summary dataclass and a parser class on bulk_ingest_document, two internal function names on batch_ingest_documents, a service method and a provider class on recompute_deferred_vault_abstracts, that same parser class on get_filename_metadata, a store class and an exception class on migrate_vault) -- and the remaining two carry pins instead, three names between them: create_vault naming a Python constructor and its class for a default config that no route returns, and Sha256Str on verify_hashes, where the alias is the published shape. The extractor gained an interior-capital tier to see them at all: shipped with two lowercase-only patterns, it bounded that very enumeration silently, which is the module's own defect class one level up. Error codes remain largely outside the relation in both directions -- the swept surfaces stop before the Error modes block, and response descriptions feed the vocabulary rather than being checked against it, so a code invented there validates itself -- recorded as a limit and carried as its own ticket. Prose corrections move on both surfaces together, the two being compared pairwise. Tests: a new gate, tests/sage/test_narrative_schema_grounding.py, asserts every identifier a narrative names is defined somewhere in the contract, over a vocabulary assembled from the machine-readable definitions rather than hand-maintained -- both specs' components, every operationId, MCP tool name and tool argument, the vault-config schema's properties followed through its sibling $refs, the error codes read out of the exception hierarchy by AST because a SAGEError subclass binds its code at instantiation, and the base lifecycle vocabulary. Its extractor is deliberately not the parity gate's, whose pattern requires an underscore and so cannot see `linearity` at all; extraction here is snake_case union single-word backticked tokens. The relation it asserts is whether a name is part of the contract, not whether it is a response field of that operation: whether prose offers an identifier as a response field is a fact about the sentence around it, and the module says so rather than implying a reach it does not have -- which also leaves the type-and-range half of the audit a human read. Forty-eight names resolve to nothing and are pinned with what they are instead (error-envelope detail fields, vault-config values, worked-example placeholders, an untyped edge-warning vocabulary, MCP-only argument values), fourteen mapped pairs resolve completely and are absent from the table, and a staleness test rejects a pin the moment its name becomes resolvable, so the set can only shrink. Anti-vacuity floors pin the extractor and the vocabulary at both ends, since either collapsing to empty would make every assertion pass. The same module also asserts no $ref in either spec dangles, which is what surfaced the eight above. test_openapi_conformance.py gains the field-level Pydantic->YAML direction and loses the sentence claiming that direction would duplicate the forward one, which those eight fields disprove.

Bound the reabstract-deferred per-document wait and report how each document settled. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.24->v0.25. ReabstractOutcome gains two members, still_skipped and timeout, taking the enum to success / skipped_pdf / llm_failure / still_skipped / timeout; the widening is the one this revision records, and the v1.22 entry that introduced the enum describes the three it shipped with. The operation description's terminal set widens from (abstraction_complete or failed) to the full vocabulary, matching sage.models.enums.TERMINAL_PIPELINE_STATUSES: the omitted abstraction_skipped left the poller waiting on a document that had already settled. A wait ceiling is added because widening the terminal set cannot bound the reachable stranding -- the abstraction worker is cancelled on lifespan teardown and on registry reload, which drops queued jobs and leaves their documents at the non-terminal abstraction_in_progress -- and a document abandoned at the ceiling is reported outcome=timeout. The recovery contract is stated rather than assumed: this operation enumerates abstraction_skipped only, so an abandoned document is reached by a later call only once startup recovery or the out-of-band bulk sweep advances it. ReabstractProgressEvent's status and outcome descriptions gain the partition (skipped carries skipped_pdf or still_skipped, failed carries llm_failure or timeout), and its error and elapsed_seconds descriptions are reconciled with it -- a still_skipped document rides the skipped status but did dispatch and wait, so it carries both fields that the prior prose said a skipped event omits. The SSE status vocabulary is unchanged, so a client switching on status alone keeps working. Pydantic models in sage/models/schemas.py mirror the description changes verbatim.

Say what a batch ingest does when the batch itself fails after the stream has opened. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.23->v0.24 and cas_app_api.openapi.yaml v0.3->v0.4 with byte-identical prose added to the batch-ingest operation description; no schema or operation shape changes, and no new event variant. Each spec already said that a per-file failure is collected into the summary rather than ending the stream, and that the 400 and 404 refusals resolve before the stream is opened; neither said what happens to a failure of the batch itself, which can only surface after the 200 is committed. The stream now ends there deterministically and by propagating: no further events, no `error` variant, and the connection closes without a `summary`, so a stream that ends without one did not complete and the `summary` event rather than the end of the stream is the completion signal. The cause is logged server-side rather than sent, because by then the response is committed -- both the staging loop and the pipeline run on the delivery generator's first step -- so every refusal that can be decided before the response opens already is, as a typed error envelope, and what is left cannot be. That also matches the only other SSE stream in the service layer, a direct generator whose exceptions propagate the same way. Code (not in this spec): sage/services/batch_ingest_stream.py enqueues the consumer's terminating sentinel unconditionally, so a pipeline that raised before reaching it no longer leaves the consumer blocked on a queue read forever with the response held open; the consumer always reaches its `await task`, which re-raises, and the exception is logged with its traceback on the way past. sage/services/batch_ingest.py collects per-file failures as BatchIngestFileError models rather than dicts shaped like them, so the non-streaming leg -- which serialized whatever the collection held -- carries the same validated contract the streaming leg got when it built its summary event; IngestSummary.to_dict serializes with exclude_none, so the dict that leg returns is unchanged, an optional field the error does not have staying absent rather than null. edge_warnings is retyped the same way and for the same reason, the argument for errors being true of it verbatim: it sits two fields away in the same dataclass, is handled two lines apart in the same to_dict and the same summary-event mapping, and was the one remaining collection the streaming leg validated and the non-streaming leg did not. EdgeResult.warnings and EdgePlan.warning carry EdgeWarning models built at the fourteen producer sites in sage/services/batch_inference.py, and to_dict serializes them with a plain model_dump rather than exclude_none, every EdgeWarning field being required. No producer was malformed, so no wire payload changes. Also in this revision: the reabstract-deferred operation, the core spec's other text/event-stream surface and the very precedent this stream's termination shape is modeled on, gains the same mid-stream-failure paragraph -- it already carried the matching sentence about its 404 and 409 refusals resolving before the stream opens, so documenting the contract for one of the two operations that share it and citing the undocumented one as justification was the gap.

Gate a tool docstring against the operation description it implements. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.22->v0.23, four operation narratives and no schema or operation shape changes. verify_preconditions' summary now reads as the tool's own summary line does, naming what is checked rather than restating it, and its description gains the outcome for a target the vault does not hold -- reported unsatisfied with actual of "not found" -- which the old summary's word "exist" was the only disclosure of. chain's description no longer claims a single round-trip: the walk is one recursive CTE whatever the chain length, followed by a query for the connecting edges, and the service adds an existence check ahead of both, so the old sentence was false on a surface an agent selecting a tool for a long chain acts on. list_staging_edges' tier-2 bullet names identifier_mention beside the superseded content_reference placeholder, keeping the "e.g." that marks the list as examples rather than the enum's six methods. chain's description also stops naming a response field that does not exist: both caller-facing narratives called it `linearity` and described it as three-valued, where the response model and the schema both declare `is_linear`, a boolean that is false for a merge as well as a fork. The schema was correct throughout and is unchanged; only the prose moved. The four tool docstrings move with them: the two surfaces are compared pairwise, so a correction to one that is not made to the other is a divergence by construction. Tests: a new gate, tests/sage/test_mcp_docstring_disclosure_parity.py, compares the two prose surfaces of a mapped pair, which nothing did before -- the argument-conformance gate compares parameter shape and the description-parity gate compares Pydantic fields against YAML properties, and neither reaches the prose on a tool. Two complementary comparisons, both bidirectional. Claims are compared by content-word coverage against the whole opposing surface, order- and length-insensitive because the two surfaces order the same rules differently and one routinely elaborates what the other states once; verbatim equality is impossible here and set equality over quoted tokens is worse than insufficient, since neither of the two divergences this gate was built for introduced a token. Polarity is the exception to the fraction: a word that inverts a claim rather than adding to it is required rather than counted, because one added negation in a seven-word rule clears any workable floor and the opposite rule would otherwise read as disclosed. It is required against the claim's counterpart sentence rather than against the opposing surface as a whole, since a whole-surface vocabulary is a set and one negation anywhere satisfies every claim at once. Word order, negations inside sub-floor fragments, and doubly-negated sentences remain outside what the relation sees, recorded in the module docstring as limits rather than left to be inferred. Names are compared exactly and by snake_case shape rather than by markup, since coverage tolerates a claim that survives almost intact. The coverage pool on each side is the narrative plus exactly the structural surfaces the other's blocks correspond to -- Args: and Error modes: against parameters[*], responses[*] and the requestBody's own descriptions -- and no further: component-schema property prose answers to its own gate, and drawing on it would make the tool-says-more direction weaker than its mirror. Enrollment is a ratchet: four pairs are held to the relation, every other mapped pair carries the divergence it had when pinned as an asserted integer equality per side, so a pinned pair may be reconciled but never widened, and a staleness test rejects a pin the moment its pair comes clean. Both historical divergences are carried as regression fixtures asserting the relation reports the drift and falls silent once reconciled, alongside controls for an injected claim, a polarity flip, a near-miss claim measured at 0.75 coverage that pins COVERAGE_FLOOR from below, and an identifier extractor that must actually extract. The published-document, verbatim-description, YAML<->Pydantic parity, MCP-tool-conformance, self-documentation, public-posture and collection-integrity gates pass with no new allowlist entries.

Identify a batch-ingest error entry by its position in the batch. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.21->v0.22 and cas_app_api.openapi.yaml v0.2->v0.3 with byte-identical component edits: BatchIngestFileError gains a required file_index (integer, minimum 0), the file's zero-based position in the batch and the same index the progress events report; ProgressEvent.file_index gains the matching minimum 0 so the two declarations of one concept carry one bound; SummaryEvent.errors' description names the position alongside the staged filename, the caller's spelling, and the message. The upload leg of the batch endpoint stages every part under one directory by basename, so two same-named parts collapsed onto one staged path and the later part replaced the earlier one's bytes before either was ingested; and because on that leg the caller's spelling is the upload's filename, two same-named parts carry identical filename and source_path by construction, so the error entry needed a field that still tells them apart. Code (not in this spec): sage/services/batch_ingest_stream.py stages each part in its own position-named subdirectory and reduces a degenerate filename through the shared staging_name helper; sage/services/batch_ingest.py emits file_index from the one entry builder both the SSE and MCP legs share; sage/models/schemas.py declares BatchFileIndex once and applies it at both sites; app/src/api/types.ts mirrors the field. Prior history this entry also records: the same component's optional code and detail properties, added to both specs when a typed refusal's code and detail were carried through the batch error envelope (v0.20 era), landed without a manifest revision; the component as of 1.65 is filename, source_path, message, file_index (required) plus code, detail (optional).

Report a source-path rewrite that leaves two records naming one stored file. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.20->v0.21: SourcePathNormalization gains path_shared_with, the other document ids holding the normalized path once the migration completes -- those that already held it, and those the same pass rewrote onto it. Empty in the ordinary case. The normalization sweep reduced a legacy spelling to its plain form without asking whether another record already held that form, and the pair for which that matters is the one the sweep exists to repair: a record spelled with a `.` segment, and the second document a re-projection landed on the same stored file before the provenance lookup consulted both spellings. Their differing spellings were the only thing keeping them apart, so the migration that reduces them is the last moment the pair can be observed at all -- a later pass sees two identical paths and cannot tell that one was ever the legacy one. Reported rather than acted on, matching the tier3-uniqueness scan it runs beside: several documents on one source path is a state the substrate allows (the durable store collapses it with DISTINCT ON, its source_path index is non-unique), and resolving it means deciding which record to keep, which is the operator's judgment. Code (not in this spec): the GraphStore port gains find_document_ids_by_source_paths, the companion of find_documents_by_source_paths rather than a variant of it -- that one collapses the several-documents-one-path case to a single representative because provenance needs one answer, while a caller asking who else holds a path needs all of them -- implemented on both bindings with ids ordered within each path. MaintenanceService._normalize_source_paths splits into plan-then-apply: every rewrite is planned, the holders are resolved once against the vault as it stood before the pass, and only then are the writes issued. The ordering is load-bearing rather than incidental: asked while rewriting, the question depends on how far the pass has got, and each of two converging records gives a different answer about the same convergence. The lookup is skipped entirely when nothing is planned, so a clean vault still asks the store exactly once. Tests: two port tests (every id per path, which is what separates the method from its DISTINCT ON sibling and needs a two-document corpus to show; and an empty request against a non-empty store), MNT-011 (a record already holding the plain form), MNT-012 (two candidates arriving at one path together -- the shape a store-only lookup misses entirely and a resolve-while-rewriting one reports on whichever id sorts second), MNT-013 (the ordinary lone rewrite reports nothing, the half the other two cannot carry since both only assert an expected id is present), MNT-014 (a store write failing for anything but a refusal propagates rather than being swallowed by a widened catch -- the seed MNT-008 lacked, which left `except VaultRootEscapeError` and `except Exception` indistinguishable), and a lookup-count assertion on the clean-vault test. The seam, verbatim-description, YAML<->Pydantic parity, router-conformance, MCP-tool-conformance and typed-alias gates pass with no new allowlist entries.

Report the repair of a stored source_path that is not in its plain form. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.19->v0.20: a new SourcePathNormalization component (document_id / previous_source_path / normalized_source_path) and a MigrationReport.source_paths_normalized array carrying one entry per record the migration rewrote; the migrate_vault operation description moves from one data backfill to two. Ingest reduces a recorded vault-relative path to one spelling on the single branch that used to store the caller's string verbatim, but records written before that still hold another -- a `.` segment, a doubled separator, or a trailing one -- and nothing brought them forward. The read side resolves such a path while the write-time guard refuses it, so the record names a location its own bytes cannot be written back to, and re-projecting it raises force_reingest_path_mismatch: the stored path genuinely differs from the computed one, which is precisely the condition the cross-document guard exists to reject, so no amount of lookup tolerance can reach it. Hence a migration rather than more tolerance. Code (not in this spec): the normalization rule moves out of the ingestion service to sage/vault_source_binding.py as the public normalize_vault_relative, beside _assert_plain_vault_relative -- the write-time shape check it exists to agree with -- and raises that module's own VaultRootEscapeError, which the ingest call site's enclosing _translate_vault_source_refusal already converts, leaving the caller-facing vault_source_path_refused unchanged. Sharing one function rather than two implementations of `plain form` is load-bearing: the rewrite's whole purpose is that the path a re-projection computes and the path the record holds stop differing, which two reductions agreeing only today would not deliver. The GraphStore port gains list_non_canonical_source_paths, mapping document id to the value the record holds for every path carrying something a plain POSIX form reduces, together with NON_CANONICAL_SOURCE_PATH_PATTERN -- one regex over the three reductions (a `.` segment bounded by a separator or an end, a doubled separator, a trailing one), written in the intersection of POSIX and Python syntax so the durable store hands it to the database and the in-memory store to `re` and the two cannot answer differently. The selection is deliberately a superset of `the plain form differs`: `.`, `/`, and anything under a `//` root match the pattern and still reduce to themselves, because POSIX leaves `//` implementation-defined and pathlib preserves it. The caller settles those by reducing and comparing. Making the predicate exact instead would mean re-encoding pathlib's `//` rule in SQL -- a second encoding of the reducer, which is the drift the shared pattern exists to prevent -- and backing the in-memory store with the reducer rather than the pattern reads as the stronger choice while being quietly narrower, omitting every `//`-rooted candidate the durable store really offers. `..` is deliberately not a selector: pathlib preserves it rather than resolving it, so such a path is already the only spelling of itself, the normalizer refuses it, and there is nothing to rewrite it to -- verify_vault_source_files already reports that condition as out_of_root, so the fact keeps one home. MaintenanceService.migrate_vault runs the sweep alongside its standing pipeline_error backfill and before the tier3-uniqueness scan, catching the normalizer's refusal per record so one unrepairable legacy path cannot fail the whole call; the write is a bare source_path field set through update_document, which stamps no updated_at -- a respelling is not a modification, and bumping it would make every record in a legacy vault read as freshly changed to the drift and staleness comparisons. The filesystem binding streams the file into place and digests it as it passes -- one read of the source and no read of the destination, since that binding stores what it is handed, so the digest of the bytes in flight is the digest of the copy at rest. The document-store binding streams the file to the store and answers with a streamed re-read of the copy, the one place that read still belongs: the store rewrites Office packages at rest and reports no SHA-256 of its own, so what it holds cannot be known from what was sent. Its Graph client's upload_source now streams from a path: a single fixed-length PUT at or below 10 MiB (Graph's simple upload accepts up to 250 MB; 10 MiB is where its documentation recommends a resumable transfer) and an upload session above it -- createUploadSession asking to replace the item, then sequential 10 MiB fragments (32 times the 320 KiB quantum Graph requires, under its 60 MiB per-request ceiling) PUT to the session URL with Content-Range and no bearer, one throttle retry per fragment re-sending the same range, and a refused fragment or a premature commit cancelling the session and failing closed. That lifts the document store's upload ceiling from the restore path, and the Graph module's docstring no longer records upload sessions as deferred. retain_source on the document-store binding sheds its own whole-file read as a consequence, with no behavioural change. restore_vault_source_file digests the delivered file in one streamed pass, hands its path to write_source, and takes the as-stored digest from the write instead of a separate hash_source round-trip; the refresh rule is unchanged, so an intact copy is still left alone and stored_content_hash moves only where the store demonstrably rewrote the bytes. Tests: VSBB-068/069/070 (the digest of what was written is returned; the file is streamed with whole-file reads forbidden; one pass over the source and never a read of the destination, by recording every open), VSB-DS-074/075 (the returned digest is what the store holds, diverging from the delivered one on a stamped package, by one streamed re-read and no download; retain_source never materializes the file), VSB-DS-076..082 (a small source is one fixed-length streamed PUT; a large one is a session of exactly ranged, unauthenticated fragments that reassemble to the file; fragment geometry honors the store's rules; a refused fragment cancels the session and fails closed; a throttled fragment is retried once with the same range; a refused session creation sends no bytes; a premature commit is an error), and two service tests (the restore streams the delivered file; the as-stored digest is taken from the write, with the copy hashed once before the write and never after).
