Make the source-file read side see a recorded path that leaves the vault's source tree. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.17->v0.18: SourceFileIntegrityEntry.integrity_status gains the value `out_of_root` alongside `missing`, `hash_mismatch` and `symlinked`, and SourceFileIntegrityReport.summary moves from four counts to five. The restore operation's description gains the matching rule beside the one it already carried for a link: a recorded path resolving outside the source tree is never reported already_intact, and the write is refused as vault_source_path_refused rather than landing outside the vault. The audit and the repair already agreed on whether a recorded path is a *link*, through one shared observation; they still disagreed on the other question the write guards ask, whether the path resolves inside the vault's source root. With the source tree's `imports/` pointing at a directory outside the root and an ordinary file behind it, source_is_symlink returns False and source_exists returns True, so the audit reported the document healthy while both write_source and retain_source refused it -- the same operator-sent-to-a-repair-that-refuses outcome the link work closed one level down the path. Containment, not linkedness, is the discriminating question there: an ancestor whose target is *inside* the root is accepted by the write side and goes on being reported healthy. An `out_of_root` row is emitted in both audit modes (establishing it is a path resolution, not a content read) and carries a null observed_content_hash: what the bytes at the end of an unwritable path hash to is not a fact about the copy the record can hold. It outranks `missing`, since the store refuses the path whether or not anything resolves at the far end, and reporting the document absent would send an operator to re-deliver content into a path that will decline it. It ranks below `symlinked`, because where the recorded path is itself a link, removing the link is the whole repair and saying so is more use than naming wherever it points. Code (not in this spec): the VaultSourceStore port gains source_is_out_of_root, the companion of source_is_symlink rather than a restatement of it -- that one asks whether the path's own final component is a link, this asks where the path as a whole lands -- implemented by both bindings. The filesystem binding answers by running write_source's own two containment guards (the vault-relative shape check and the realpath containment resolve) and reporting whether either refuses, so the answer a caller reads and the verdict a write would receive cannot drift apart. The document-store binding answers from the path shape alone, without a store call: it has no local tree for a resolver to walk and its client's URL builder joins segments verbatim, so the shape check is the whole of the port's containment promise on that side and exactly what its write_source refuses on. Unlike that binding's source_is_symlink the answer is not a constant, and it is scoped to the key as the other is scoped to the leaf: a folder shortcut standing in for a segment on the way to a key is not answered there. The shared _RetainedCopyObservation gains an out_of_root field that suppresses `intact` outright, so the audit's new status and the repair's refusal come from one look rather than two hand-kept copies: the restore no longer reports already_intact for such a path however its bytes hash, and the write it then attempts is refused by the binding's existing guard. The field stays separate from `symlinked` rather than folding into one unwritability fact, because the two call for different remedies -- a link is removed, a path leaving the tree is re-pointed or the vault reconfigured -- and neither implies the other. Presence is kept alongside it rather than collapsed, as it is behind a link: once the path is brought back inside the tree, whether the content is still there decides whether a re-delivery is needed on top of that. The ingest reuse short-circuit gains the same conjunct, so a re-delivery no longer hands back a path every later read follows out of the tree. Behaviour is unchanged for every retained copy whose path resolves inside the source root, including one reached through an ancestor that resolves back into it. Tests: VSBB-062/063/064/065 (the port method reports a regular file under an out-of-root ancestor, accepts an ancestor resolving back inside the root, answers False for both paths the binding itself writes and for an absent in-root path, and reports the absolute and `..`-bearing shapes), VSBB-066 (the containment answer and write_source's refusal agree across all four verdicts -- the drift this change exists to close, one level up), VSB-DS-073 (the document-store binding answers from the shape without a store call, and not by a constant), service coverage for an out-of-root path holding correct bytes in hash and existence modes, an absent one classified out_of_root rather than missing, an in-root ancestor link left healthy (the case that separates asking where a path resolves from asking whether reaching it crosses a link), the five-way summary partition over a mixed vault, the restore refusing such a path and leaving it untouched (pinned by modification time, since the delivered bytes are the target's own), the intact predicate refusing an observation carrying a matching digest, the audit and restore both believing one faked observation, and VSBB-067 (a forced re-delivery refuses rather than reusing an out-of-root path). The seam, verbatim-description, YAML<->Pydantic parity, router-conformance, MCP-tool-conformance, surface-partition, and typed-alias gates pass with no new allowlist entries: the seam gate derives its surface from the port's abstract set, so the new method is picked up automatically and required of both bindings.

Add an in-place source-file restore to the maintenance surface, and retire the redundant digest of a delivered source. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml bumped v0.13->v0.14: new operation maint_restore_vault_source_file (POST /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/admin/restore-source-file) with new component schemas SourceFileRestoreRequest (source; optional document_id) and SourceFileRestoreReport (vault_id, document_id, source_path, status of restored|already_intact, provenance_verified, record_refreshed, expected_content_hash, observed_content_hash, stored_content_hash). The two booleans report what the operation could and did not establish: provenance_verified is false only for a pinned restore of a record carrying no stored digest, where nothing on the record can confirm the delivered file; record_refreshed is false where the recorded digest was deliberately left alone, so a restore can report success while the record still describes a different copy. The operation declares 400s for a pinned target the delivered bytes do not belong to, a non-absolute source, and a recorded source_path that cannot be written where it names. The operation is the repair counterpart of maint_verify_vault_source_files, which reports a retained copy that changed outside SAGE but cannot fix one: re-ingesting cannot stand in, because retention sees only that the offered bytes differ from what sits at its target -- indistinguishable from a name collision -- so it homes the document at a second path and leaves the damaged copy in place. The restore writes at the path the record already names and never re-homes the document. SAGE retains no pristine second copy of a source, so the caller delivers the bytes and the target is resolved from their digest against recorded provenance; document_id is an optional pin for the ambiguous case (several documents sharing a provenance digest) and for records predating the provenance/stored-digest split, whose provenance digest describes the stored copy rather than the delivered bytes. An already-matching copy is left untouched (status already_intact) rather than rewritten, which under a store that restamps Office packages at rest would churn the recorded digest for no repair; where a write does happen the copy is re-read and stored_content_hash follows it only where the store demonstrably rewrote the bytes: a store that returns what it was handed licenses no digest update, so delivering the wrong file leaves the mismatch reported rather than adopting it as the expected state. Provenance, describing bytes that did not change, is never touched. A document_id pin selects which copy to repair and does not license writing arbitrary bytes there -- the delivered digest is checked against the pinned document's provenance, exempting only a pre-split record whose provenance describes its stored copy. write_source refuses an absolute or tree-escaping path on both bindings, and on the filesystem binding both write paths -- the repair and retention's own copy -- refuse a symlinked destination through one shared check applied at each of retention's exits: the path about to be written, and the path returned by the identical-content reuse branch, which writes nothing but would otherwise hand back a link as the document's own source_path -- every read following it wherever its owner points, and a later repair refusing the very path the record names. A containment resolve accompanies both, so a symlinked ancestor cannot land the copy outside the tree while the returned vault-relative path claims it is inside. A link at the planned path whose content differs is untouched: that branch disambiguates to a fresh name and never writes through it. Following such a link writes where the binding did not intend: to a second document's retained copy for a link into the tree, or, for a dangling link (which reports absent, so no collision handling engages), to a file created outside the vault entirely while the returned vault-relative path claims the bytes are inside it. Repair is deliberately not something an ingest does: an ingest that silently restored would erase the operator's evidence that something other than SAGE wrote to the store. Code (not in this spec): the VaultSourceStore port gains write_source (caller-named vault-relative path, create-or-replace, no naming rule and no collision handling), implemented by both bindings -- the filesystem binding writing under a containment guard against the vault's source root with the same UI-invisibility stripping retention applies, the document-store binding as a direct upload to the named key. retain_source gains an optional delivered_hash carrying the canonical digest a caller already computed, so an ingest digests the delivered file once instead of once to establish content identity and again inside retention; the parameter defaults to computing, keeping the port satisfiable by its weakest binding, and both bindings now derive the collision-disambiguation suffix through one shared helper and compare full canonical digests rather than 8-character truncations. The document-store binding's collision check no longer downloads the stored copy to hash it locally, using the streamed hash_source_bytes instead -- a whole-file network round-trip removed from every name-collision retain. The MCP verb taxonomy anchored to CAS-ADR-033 gains `restore`, joining the maintenance-only outliers `reload`/`migrate`/`optimize`: returning a retained source file to a state it previously held is not a partial record update, a re-derivation from inputs the substrate still holds, or a read-only assertion about state -- the bytes come from outside and overwrite what the store currently has. A binding's refusal to write at a path is translated to a typed 400 on both the repair and the ingest path, so it reaches callers as vault_source_path_refused rather than as a generic internal error or a bare 500; it is declared on the ingest operation as well as the repair, and carries the binding's own reason, since the refusal has four causes and a fixed message describes one. The one ingest branch that recorded the caller's relative string verbatim now normalizes it and consults both spellings when reading back provenance, so a record written before that change is found rather than missed -- a miss silently landed a second document on the same stored file. Tests: service-level restore coverage for a drifted copy, an intact copy, a missing copy, unclaimed bytes, an ambiguous match with and without the pin, and landing at the recorded path; VSBB-027/028/029 and VSB-DS-067 (the threaded digest is consumed rather than recomputed, proved with a deliberately wrong digest), VSBB-030/031 (one digest of the delivered file per ingest), VSBB-032/033/034 and VSB-DS-070 (write_source lands in place, creates parents, and refuses to escape the source root), read/hash counters on the document-store collision path, MPI-017 (restore repairs a drifted copy under both bindings, with the stored digest following a restamped copy), and MCP boundary coverage for the new tool. The seam, verbatim-description, YAML<->Pydantic parity, router-conformance, MCP-tool-conformance, surface-partition, typed-alias, and public-posture gates pass. Path-handling coverage: a link at the disambiguated destination and a symlinked ancestor are each refused by the guard that alone catches them, an in-tree link at the planned path still collision-handles as it always did, an absolute path inside the storage root is refused on shape where containment would accept it, a pinned restore of a diverged record accepts the correct bytes, and an ingest-path refusal surfaces as a typed envelope.

Require Document.lifecycle_status rather than letting a model default shadow the configured ingest landing state. CAS-ADR-047 is the governing decision: lifecycle preconditions derive from vault configuration, and engine literals survive only as the defaults an unset declaration resolves to. A model-level default is not such a literal -- it is reachable with no declaration at all, so any construction path that omitted the field inherited `active` whatever the vault declared, and nothing raised: the document simply came to rest in a declared state that this vault's ingest never produces, which no subsequent precondition flags as wrong. sage/models/schemas.py drops default="active"; DocumentWithContent inherits the change. The removal is not justified as a substrate-conformance fix: sage_core_api.openapi.yaml does list lifecycle_status in Document.required, but per the rationale recorded at tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py the two notions of required do not map -- OpenAPI's means the property always appears in the serialized JSON, which a defaulted field satisfies -- so the prior default was not a divergence from the YAML, and the same reading applies to the non-optional field in app/src/api/types.ts. No schema file moves. DocumentSummary.lifecycle_status was already required and is unchanged. tests/sage/test_lifecycle_status_default_guard.py pins the behavioural pair (a model that neither invents a state when none is given nor overrides one that is) and a structural gate holding the no-default property for every non-nullable lifecycle_status field in sage.models.schemas, nullability separating a state a record asserts from a filter whose absence means `any`. The gate does not reach model_construct, which bypasses validation by design where a repair workflow must read values the request-side validators reject.

Close the CAS-ADR-020 clause (f) type-restating opener at decoding time, where the bounded post-generation excision cannot reach. sage/sage_core_config.schema.json bumped v0.10->v0.11: the `abstraction` block gains `opener_constraint` (boolean, default false), selecting whether the local MLX provider constrains decoding against the clause (f) opener; Pydantic StackAbstractionConfig in sage/config.py mirrors the description verbatim (Principle 8). The mechanism is a decoding-time constraint rather than further prompt wording, which CAS-ADR-020 records as measured-unhelpful. sage/adapters/abstraction_utils.py gains the pure automaton (`forbidden_opener_continuations`, `opener_sentence_terminated`) reading the same `_DEICTIC_SUBJECT` / `_CLASSIFYING_VERBS` / `_COMPLEMENT_BREAKERS` / `_DOC_TYPE_EXPANSIONS` registries the detector reads, via a new shared `_type_phrase_candidates`, so the constraint's extent is the detector's by construction; only the final word of a candidate type phrase is forbidden, at positions a licensed complement window admits, and both the fresh-word and mid-word readings are returned so subword pieces are walked rather than prefix-blocked. sage/adapters/abstraction_qwen3.py gains `_build_surface_index` (one vocabulary pass mapping normalized surfaces to token ids, built lazily and cleared in unload alongside the template-overhead cache), `_OpenerConstraint` (an mlx-lm logits_processors callable that watermarks the prompt prefix on its first invocation, decodes only the generated suffix, and latches closed once the opening sentence terminates), and `_suppress_logits`; `_generate_sync` passes `logits_processors=` as a kwarg only when the constraint is enabled and the document carries a doc_type, leaving the prompt byte-identical. A fresh processor per generation preserves the determinism property the abstraction path is tested on. sage/mcp_init.py gains `_reject_opener_constraint_for_non_local`, modelled on the context_window rejection and applied on both the local and cloud bindings: the constraint is a property of a sampling loop a hosted provider does not expose, so clause (f) prevention is local-only while detection and the bounded repair stay provider-neutral -- an asymmetry stated in config rather than discovered later. scripts/benchmark_abstraction.py gains `--opener-constraint {off,on}` as an axis distinct from the prompt-construction arms (it changes what the sampler may select, not what the prompt says; refused against --model stub, which loads no tokenizer) and `--ids-file`, which reads an audit manifest as the corpus so the two arms measure the same documents; BenchmarkResult gains `opener_constraint`, serialized to the raw JSON and rendered on the scorecard. strip_type_restating_opener's docstring is qualified: an unconstrained regeneration still reproduces the same opening, but a constrained one is a correction, so stored text may be reached that way; the excision remains the only remedy for output already stored and for providers with no decoding surface. Tests: tests/sage/test_abstraction_opener_constraint.py (blocked and silent shapes, a parametrized extent test asserting the constraint blocks a surface exactly when the detector would flag it, and registry-growth tests that fail if the constraint carries a copy of either registry rather than reading it); tests/sage/test_abstraction_qwen3_opener_constraint.py (surface index, processor watermark/short-circuit/masking, and the provider wiring including prompt-identity and per-call-processor guards); STK-015..018 in test_stack_abstraction_dispatch.py; benchmark CLI wiring for both new flags. Two engine assumptions that a freshly ingested document is `active` are closed, leaving no schema change. (1) The LifecycleConfig validator gains its first advisory class -- logged in both the strict and lenient modes, rejecting in neither -- for an ingest landing state that no `supersede` transition leaves. Such a document is not supersedable until it is transitioned out, so ingesting with a predecessor and version-chain edge inference both refuse against it; naming that at configuration time beats discovering it later as refused chain edges. It advises rather than rejects because CAS-ADR-047 sanctions a review-style landing state, and refusing one would make unconstructible through the write surfaces exactly what a configuration is entitled to declare. (2) Identifier-mention resolution no longer prefers candidates by an `active` literal. The preferred pool is now `LifecycleConfig.supersession_surviving_states()` -- the declared states a supersession does not leave a document in, the complement of `TransitionTable.landing_states("supersede")`. A vault landing ingest outside the base lifecycle's choice thereby resolves mentions to its fresh documents, and under the base lifecycle a chain with a completed head no longer empties the preference and fall through to whichever version was stamped most recently -- which, because a supersession stamps the predecessor last, was the retired one. The batch-inference and retrieval active-state filters are unchanged, per the carve-out CAS-ADR-047 records. Cross-array invariants of this kind remain loader-owned: `sage/lifecycle.schema.json` stays at 0.3.

Lifecycle-configuration load validation covers every transition endpoint and the dependency-satisfying set, and one renderer serves every config-derived state-set precondition. (1) sage/lifecycle.schema.json 0.2 -> 0.3: from_state and to_state gain identifier patterns -- to_state is always a real state ('(new)' is the ingestion pseudo-state and no transition may land in it), from_state is that or the '(new)' literal -- and the schema description now states which invariants it carries and which the loader owns alone. (2) The LifecycleConfig validator gains two unconditional rules: every transition endpoint must name a declared state (subsuming the former '(new)'-row-only check), because a transition into an undeclared state strands the document with no valid action out; and no lifecycle may resolve to an empty dependency-satisfying set, which would fail every depends_on precondition permanently with nothing naming the configuration as the cause. Both ride the established strictness split -- the vault-create and update-config paths reject, on-disk configurations warn and load so a vault stays reachable for repair. A lifecycle that replaces the base set entirely must now declare satisfies_dependency on at least one state, since it inherits no engine default. (3) A shared render_state_set renders every caller-facing lifecycle state set: sorted, ' or '-joined, with one documented placeholder '(none)' for the empty set. The check_preconditions payload, the supersede_target_not_active error, and the refused-supersede inference warning all render through it, replacing three divergent inline renderings. The error's ['active'] empty-set fallback is removed: a table permitting supersede from no state now reports an empty allowed_states and a required_state of '(none)' rather than naming a state the vault does not permit. sage_core_api.openapi.yaml, the ingestion router description, and the MCP tool docstring state the empty case in lockstep. Tests: tests/sage/test_lifecycle_config_validation.py, tests/sage/test_state_set_rendering.py, tests/sage/test_dependency_satisfaction_config_driven.py.

Two lifecycle preconditions move from code literals into the vault configuration, and the lifecycle schema's inert constraint becomes an enforced contract. (1) sage/lifecycle.schema.json 0.1 -> 0.2: the states/items object gains satisfies_dependency (boolean|null, default null) -- whether documents in the state satisfy inbound depends_on preconditions, with null deferring to the engine default (active and completed satisfy). GraphOps check_preconditions derives its satisfying set and its required-string payload from the declared states instead of a hardcoded frozenset, so a vault can opt a domain state in or a base state out. (2) The transitions array now expresses the structural ingestion-row invariants directly: exactly one '(new)' row (contains with minContains/maxContains 1) whose action is 'ingest', with 'ingest' reserved to that row (item-level conditionals), so a config that would make ingest user-invocable or leave the landing state undefined fails schema validation. The remaining invariants -- the '(new)' row landing in a declared state, and the base_states_required promise (base states declared, each base action used by at least one transition) -- are enforced by a LifecycleConfig model validator. Strictness is contextual: the vault-create and update-config API paths reject a violating configuration (the vault keeps its previous config), while load_vault_config validates on-disk files leniently, logging each problem and loading anyway so an existing vault stays registered and reachable for repair. base_states_required drops its unenforced const:true and both descriptions state the enforced contract. (3) The ingest landing state becomes readable: TransitionTable captures the '(new)' row's target (without making ingest user-invocable) and exposes ingest_landing_state(), which raises rather than guessing when no row was declared; IngestionService lands new documents there instead of hardcoding active. (4) Description corrections in sage_core_api.openapi.yaml with lockstep Pydantic mirrors (Principle 8): IngestRequest.predecessor_id no longer hardcodes the supersede landing state as archived (it names the table-derived landing, archived under the base lifecycle); PreconditionCheck.required documents the derived-from-config contract; the verify_preconditions operation description now states the actual pipeline gate (not failed -- a mid-pipeline target is not rejected) instead of overclaiming a terminal-status requirement; the LifecycleStatus enum description no longer asserts the base set is unconditionally present. MCP tool docstrings for ingest_document, create_edges, and verify_preconditions follow, as do the tests/sage/contract_tests.md minimal-baseline inputs (VC-001/VC-002 declare base_states_required: false, matching what the loader accepts). Tests: tests/sage/test_dependency_satisfaction_config_driven.py, tests/sage/test_ingest_landing_state_table_driven.py, tests/sage/test_lifecycle_config_validation.py.

Each item is dispatched through GraphOpsService.link_idempotent so the prior natural-key idempotency contract is preserved: a duplicate triple (source_id, target_id, edge_type) returns the existing edge with created=false rather than raising. The batch is NOT atomic (CAS-ADR-029): a per-item SAGEError is wrapped via sage_error_to_envelope and surfaced inside the response while earlier-or-later successful items remain committed. response_mode follows the sibling bulk tools (/): 'light' drops the per-item edge body from success entries; the created and existing_rationale fields are preserved under light because they are the only natural-key idempotency signals; default-resolution rule is >5 items → light. dry_run (/) propagates envelope-level to per-item LinkRequest construction; the per-item edge.id carries the nil-UUID sentinel on the create path or the existing edge id on a natural-key hit. Unlike the document-patch bulk tools, BulkLinkItemResult carries no `changes` block — link is an edge mutation, not a document field patch, so the would-be edge IS the change surface (matching create_edge's single-item precedent). Adds a `dry_run: bool = False` parameter to the request schemas of `update_metadata`, `bulk_update_metadata`, `update_lifecycle`, `bulk_update_lifecycle`, `create_edge`, and `update_vault_config` (and as a method/query parameter on `delete_edge`, which has no request body). When set, each tool runs every validator in the same order as a real run but skips persistence at the storage call site — no document or edge write, no `metadata_confirmed` flip, no `updated_at` advance, no chunk-store sync, no yaml write, no registry reload. Three new response wrappers and one preview model: `UpdateMetadataResponse` and `LinkResponse` promote the previously-bare `Document` and `Edge` returns so the `dry_run` echo has a home (breaking change on those two single-item paths; bulk-result envelopes, `SetLifecycleResponse`, `UnlinkResponse`, and `UpdateVaultConfigResponse` are extended in place); `VaultConfigPreview` carries the section-level diff returned on `update_vault_config` dry-run. Per-edge non-persistence is marked by the nil-UUID sentinel `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` on would-be `created_edge` (supersede) and would-be `edge.id` (link); the validator on `EdgeIdStr` accepts it because it's a syntactically-valid UUID, and `uuid4` cannot mint it, so a caller that mistakes it for a real id fails loudly on lookup. Three site-specific decisions worth recording: (1) the prior natural-key pre-check is dry-run-only — real-run still relies on the storage uniqueness constraint, preserving the executor-submission bound from the earlier change; on dry-run, the pre-check lifts the gap to the application layer so the no-op outcome is reported faithfully (same shape as the real-run no-op path under `link_idempotent`). (2) `update_vault_config` dry-run NEVER raises `destructive_config_change`; warnings always appear in the response body so the caller can plan a follow-up real-run with `force=true`. `force` is a no-op on dry-run. (3) For supersede, `SetLifecycleResponse.created_edge` is populated on both real-run and dry-run so the field has uniform semantics — the real `id` is non-deterministic at commit time; on dry-run it carries the sentinel. Bulk tools propagate envelope `dry_run` to per-item construction; per-item override is forbidden by design. Documented limitation in the bulk docstrings: each item's dry-run is evaluated against the committed state at batch start, so item N's would-be effects are NOT visible to item N+1 (the field-report scenario: add tag X in item N, try to add the same tag in item N+1 — both report success in dry-run, the second fails on real-run). Internal `link_idempotent` callers (`batch_inference`, `identifier_mention_inference`) keep the existing `(Edge, bool)` tuple return; only the public `link` and the MCP-tool wrapper return `LinkResponse`, minimizing the wrapper-promotion blast radius. New tests at tests/sage/test_update_metadata_dry_run.py, test_set_lifecycle_dry_run.py (incl. supersede), test_link_dry_run.py (incl. the prior natural-key collision), test_unlink_dry_run.py, test_update_vault_config_dry_run.py (incl. destructive-change case), test_bulk_dry_run.py (incl. per-item independence documented limitation). Shared helpers `state_snapshot` and `assert_state_unchanged` at tests/sage/_dry_run_helpers.py provide the universal 'no state was written' proof (snapshot documents + edges + chunk pushdown fields + optional yaml mtime/size; surfaces per-field diff on failure). The OpenAPI conformance suite (test_openapi_conformance.py) passes including the verbatim Pydantic↔YAML description-sync gate; the test_openapi_conformance suite is the parity enforcer for the new schemas and the modified field descriptions on `UnlinkResponse` and `UpdateVaultConfigResponse`.

Unify response_mode across search targets and deprecate response_level (follow-up). Six changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) New DocumentSummaryLight component schema with five properties (id, title, lifecycle_status, doc_type, tier3_metadata) — the stripped shape returned by search when target=documents, mode=catalog, response_mode=light. (2) DiscoverHit.document switched from a single $ref to DocumentSummary to a oneOf<DocumentSummary, DocumentSummaryLight>; full-mode and non-catalog paths still produce DocumentSummary, the new union accommodates the catalog-light stripped variant without weakening the full contract. (3) DiscoverRequest.response_level made nullable with default null (was default 'chunks') and description rewritten to lead with [DEPRECATED] and a worked equivalence map to response_mode. (4) DiscoverRequest.response_mode description rewritten to describe unified cross-target semantics (the previous text scoped the parameter to target=edges only). (5) Validator behavior change in sage/models/schemas.py: the prior branch that rejected response_mode + target=documents is removed; a new branch raises mode_parameter_mismatch when response_mode and response_level are passed together on target=documents (the two now resolve to the same selector via a precedence rule in the retrieval service, so allowing both would let a caller request a conflicting shape). (6) Service-layer wiring in sage/services/retrieval.py: _catalog routes through a new _project_doc_summary helper that returns DocumentSummaryLight for response_mode=light and DocumentSummary otherwise; _results_to_hits resolves include_content from response_mode first, falling back to response_level when only the legacy parameter is set. The >5-results default-to-light threshold rule stays edge-only by design: discover is general-purpose tooling called from every dashboard load; silently flipping the default catalog response shape for existing callers is a backward-compat hazard the threshold rule was never meant to introduce on documents. The asymmetry against the prior bulk endpoints (which DO opt into the threshold default) is in the use case, not the parameter contract: bulk endpoints are batch-by-construction. MCP tool surface: search.response_level signature changed from str='chunks' to str|None=None so callers that omit the parameter don't trip the new mutual-exclusion check when also passing response_mode; the response_mode docstring section is rewritten to carry the four-mode behavior matrix. the prior response_mode rejection test is deleted; new tests at tests/sage/test_retrieval.py cover validator acceptance, mutual exclusion, catalog stripped-vs-full semantics, semantic/keyword light/full equivalence, deterministic ignored, no-threshold-on-documents, and a deprecation-marker guard on the Pydantic Field description. Removal of response_level itself is deferred to a follow-up ticket once external callers have migrated.

Add response_mode parameter to bulk mutation tools (follow-up). Six changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) BulkLifecycleRequest gains an optional response_mode property ($ref to the existing ResponseMode component, nullable) selecting per-item payload depth on the bulk lifecycle endpoint. (2) BulkMetadataRequest gains the same optional response_mode property on the bulk metadata endpoint. (3) BulkLifecycleItemResult.document description extended to note that the field is absent on success entries when response_mode=light, in addition to its existing absence on error entries. (4) BulkMetadataItemResult.document description extended the same way. (5) ResponseMode component description rewritten to reflect its cross-surface scope (previously phrased as edges-only on search); the per-surface light-mode shape distinction is now explicit. (6) MCP tool surface: bulk_update_lifecycle and bulk_update_metadata both gain response_mode: str|None=None signature parameter and corresponding docstring sections; the parameter forwards into the Request model where Pydantic enforces the enum. Service layer (sage/services/lifecycle.py, sage/services/metadata.py): both bulk methods resolve effective_mode via len(items) > LIGHT_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD when response_mode is unset, then skip populating the per-item document field on success entries when mode is LIGHT; failure entries continue to carry the full structured error envelope regardless of mode. Constant hoist: _LIGHT_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD moved from sage/services/retrieval.py to sage/models/enums.py as the public LIGHT_DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, importable by services that honor the same default-resolution rule. The threshold-default stance for bulk endpoints is deliberately the opposite of the prior decision for search documents: bulk endpoints are batch-by-construction (the >5 case is the surface's primary use case, not an ambient-caller shape change), so the threshold-default automatically engages on the bulk surface where keeps it off the documents-discover surface. Tests at tests/sage/test_sage_bulk_set_lifecycle.py, test_sage_bulk_update_metadata.py, test_bulk_lifecycle_router.py, and test_bulk_metadata_router.py each gain nine cases (T1 explicit light strips document and semantic_abstract; T2 explicit full preserves them; T3 default above threshold returns light; T4 default at-or-below threshold returns full; T5 error envelope intact in light; T6 error envelope intact in full; T7 mixed-result batch in light; T8 invalid response_mode rejected up front with no per-item state change; T9 empty batch with explicit light). The OpenAPI conformance suite (test_openapi_conformance.py) passes for the prior description surface.

Initial draft. Ten configuration schemas across SAGE (6) and ROOT Harness (4), covering all twelve items in the ROOT Harness instantiation checklist. JSON Schema draft 2020-12. API operation contracts deferred to v0.2. Developed against SAGE Architecture Reference v1.3 and ROOT Harness Architecture Reference v0.5.

API contracts and data model schemas. Added five artifacts resolving all deferred items from v0.1: (1) SAGE Core API OpenAPI specification (sage/sage_core_api.openapi.yaml), 14 operations across 7 tags, developed against SAGE Architecture Reference v1.4 Section 7. (2) ROOT Harness Orchestration API OpenAPI specification (root_harness/orchestration_api.openapi.yaml), 9 operations across 5 tags, developed against ROOT Harness Architecture Reference v1.0 Section 2.5. SAGE tier 2 behavioral design decisions applied to schemas. Seven changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml and vault_config.schema.json: (1) Document.indexed_at changed from required to nullable (null until indexing completes). (2) Document.pipeline_error added as nullable string (failure description when pipeline_status is failed). (3) Edge.id added as required auto-generated field (enables duplicate edge disambiguation). (4) TraversalNode.edge_count added (deduplication signal for traversal results). (5) IngestRequest.force added as boolean (bypasses duplicate detection for pipeline failure recovery). (6) SetLifecycleResponse schema added with optional warnings array (pipeline status advisory). (7) vault_config.schema.json: retrieval_health section added with assertions_file field. Also added 409 duplicate content response to ingest endpoint. Updated abstraction.enabled description to reflect strict quality gate decision (LLM failure = failed, not skipped).

Edge inference schema support. Three changes for the CAS Application's filename-aware scan and bulk ingest workflow: (1) metadata_extraction.schema.json: added known_code_patterns (regex list for code segment recognition during tolerant filename parsing, independent of doc_type mapping) and keyword_to_doc_type (keyword-based doc_type mapping evaluated before code_to_doc_type, resolves mis-classification of workflow artifacts containing domain-specific codes). Updated filename_extraction description to document tolerant parser behavior. Updated code_to_doc_type description to clarify evaluation order relative to keyword_to_doc_type. (2) sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: added metadata property to IngestRequest (optional string-valued object for caller-supplied metadata fields from parsed filename segments, participates in standard precedence chain). Enables single-call ingestion with metadata instead of separate ingest + update_metadata.

Catalog mode and discovery improvements. Three changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) RetrievalMode enum: added 'catalog' (filter-only SQL enumeration, no vector search, returns document metadata only) and 'keyword' (BM25-only search, was in code but missing from spec). (2) DiscoverRequest: added 'offset' integer property (pagination for catalog mode, default 0). Updated description to document all five modes. (3) RetrievalFilters: added 'pipeline_status' string property (was in code but missing from spec; overrides default failed-pipeline exclusion).

Document-level response mode and catalog sort parameters. Six additions to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) ResponseLevel enum (chunks, documents) controlling result detail level. (2) DiscoverRequest.response_level property (default 'chunks'); when set to 'documents', suppresses chunk_content but preserves heading_path (best chunk's location) and relevance scores. Applicable to semantic and keyword modes; ignored by catalog and deterministic. (3) DiscoverHit.matched_chunk_count (nullable integer): number of chunks from the document that matched the query, useful as a reranking signal. (4) CatalogSortBy enum (title, doc_type, document_date, lifecycle_status) for catalog mode sorting. (5) SortOrder enum (asc, desc). (6) DiscoverRequest.sort_by and sort_order properties for catalog mode. Sort_by and sort_order were in code since v1.3 but missing from the OpenAPI spec.

Chain walk endpoint and edge-type breakdown. Three changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) New POST /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/chain endpoint with ChainRequest, ChainResponse, and ChainEntry schemas. Walks an edge chain to both ends from any starting document via recursive CTE, returning an ordered list with head_id, tail_id, query_position, length, and is_linear (fork detection). Designed for version history retrieval on long supersedes chains but works with any edge type. (2) TraversalNode.edge_count (integer) replaced by edge_counts (object, additionalProperties: integer). Per-type edge count map keyed by edge type string. Breaking change from scalar to map. (3) TraversalNode.required updated from [document, edge, depth, edge_count] to [document, edge, depth, edge_counts].

Semantic abstract consumers (CAS-ADR-011). Two changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) DocumentSummary: added semantic_abstract (nullable string) so discover results carry the LLM-generated abstract without a separate get_document call. Enables steward agent orientation and vault-steward discovery as primary consumers. (2) DiscoverRequest: added use_abstract_prefilter (boolean, default true) enabling two-pass abstract-boosted retrieval in semantic and keyword modes. Documents whose abstract matches the query receive a multiplicative score boost; documents without abstracts remain discoverable at natural chunk-relevance scores.

Chain-scoped edge resolution with anchor and retraction primitives (CAS-ADR-017). New schema sage/edge_type_registry.schema.json: per-vault registry assigning a resolution_policy (none / transitive_source / transitive_both / TBD) to every edge type used by the vault; frozen per-edge at creation. Four changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) EdgeType enum extended with instantiated_from (live-tracking derivation, e.g., template instantiation), retracts (meta-edge disclaiming an earlier edge instance), and merged_from (meta-edge recording chain absorption with downstream tombstoning). (2) ResolutionPolicy enum added. (3) Edge schema extended with resolution_policy (required; frozen copy of registry value at creation), source_valid_from_version, target_valid_from_version, valid_until_version, and retracted_edge_id (all nullable); target_id made nullable to accommodate retracts edges. (4) LinkRequest schema extended with the same anchor and retracted_edge_id fields; write-time validation enforces the policy-keyed invariant and produces new 400 error codes EDGE_ANCHOR_POLICY_VIOLATION, RETRACT_TARGET_NOT_EDGE, MERGED_FROM_VALIDATION, TBD_POLICY_EDGE. (5) TraverseRequest: added debug boolean (default false). (6) TraverseResponse: added resolution_path (nullable array). (7) New ResolutionPathEntry schema discriminated by event_type (anchor_hit, anchor_miss, retracts_applied, tombstone_applied). sage/edge_inference.schema.json: edge_type enum extended with the three new values for consistency.

CAS-ADR-017 conformance alignment. (1) ResolutionPolicy enum gains transitive_target value in both sage_core_api.openapi.yaml and sage/edge_type_registry.schema.json, restoring the four-value resolution enumeration mandated by the ADR ({none, transitive_source, transitive_target, transitive_both}; TBD remains as a governance placeholder). transitive_target is the policy-level mirror of transitive_source: target anchor must lie in the queried document's lineage; source endpoint is frozen at derivation with source_valid_from_version null. No built-in edge type maps to this policy today; vaults opting into it via edge_type_registry now have a resolver and validator that honor it. (2) ResolutionPolicy description refined in the OpenAPI spec to document the null-means-not-applicable semantics for transitive_source (target_valid_from_version null) and transitive_target (source_valid_from_version null).

Intentional-ingestion constraint applied to source_adapters schema (CAS-ADR-018). Two changes to sage/source_adapters.schema.json: (1) Removed the watch_paths property from per-adapter config. SAGE provides no file watcher, polling loop, or auto-ingest; the field was a forward-declared slot for an unimplemented capability that the ADR now formally excludes. (2) Updated file_extensions description from 'Used by the file watcher and bulk ingestion' to 'Used by directory scans and bulk ingestion' to reflect the actual consumer surface (list_directory / bulk_ingest_document / ingest_document).

OpenAPI conformance backfill closing principle-8 drift on the SAGE Core and CAS Application HTTP surfaces. (1) New file cas_app_api.openapi.yaml: 2 endpoints (POST /app/scan, POST /app/ingest), 8 component schemas covering scan request/response, ingest request, and SSE progress/summary event payloads. Architecturally separate from sage_core_api so that /app/* endpoints (CAS Application workflow tools) and /sage_vaults/* endpoints (SAGE Core graph operations) are documented in distinct specs. (2) sage_core_api.openapi.yaml backfilled with 14 endpoint definitions that existed in code but had no spec entry: vault listing and creation (GET/POST /sage_vaults), vault stats (GET /stats including the lancedb_chunk_count field added 2026-04-29), vault config get/put, hash-check, staging-edges list/confirm/dismiss, pending-metadata list, document open / projection / section reads, and edge unlink (DELETE /edges/{edge_id}). 17 new component schemas (VaultSummary and sub-types, VaultStatsResponse, HealthIndicators, CreateVaultRequest, UpdateVaultConfigRequest/Response, HashCheckRequest, HashCheckMatch, StagingEdge, StagingEdgeConfirmResponse, StagingEdgeDismissResponse, ExtractedField, PendingMetadataItem, ReadProjectionResponse, ReadSectionResponse, OpenDocumentResponse, UnlinkResponse). Three new tag entries (Vault Management, Staging Edges, Pending Metadata). Preamble corrected: the no-delete invariant applies to documents only (per SAGE Architecture Reference §6.4); edges may be removed via unlink. (3) Editor endpoints (GET/PUT /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/documents/{document_id}/editors) confirmed as architecturally intentional forward declarations per SAGE Architecture Reference §4.3 and §6.3 -- left in spec, allowlisted in conformance test as pending implementation. (4) Conformance enforcement: tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py defines five tests (path/method coverage with both specs aggregated, response schemas non-stub per spec, OpenAPI 3.1 validity per spec, VaultStatsResponse documents lancedb_chunk_count, URL-prefix boundary between specs). All seven test cases pass; coincidental-pass check verified each new test fails when its driver state is reverted.

Caller-owned metadata inference and review (CAS-ADR-021) -- substrate surface. Three changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) IngestRequest gains needs_review (boolean, default false). When false, SAGE skips filename inference and commits caller-supplied metadata as authoritative with metadata_confirmed=true; when true, current filename-inference + pending-metadata behavior is preserved end-to-end. Default flips from the prior implicit 'review unless caller-confirms' model to 'commit unless caller-asks-for-review'; CAS app's bulk ingest call site is updated to pass needs_review=true explicitly in the coordinated ADR-021 cleanup. (2) New endpoint POST /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/parse-filename with ParseFilenameRequest (filename + adapter) and ParseFilenameResponse (nullable title, project, version_label, document_date, doc_type, codes). Side-effect-free wrapper around the vault's FilenameParser; intended for callers that want filename-based suggestions to populate a UI before submitting an ingest with caller-authoritative metadata. New path is allowlisted in tests/sage/test_openapi_conformance.py as a forward declaration until ADR-021 implementation Chunk 3 lands the FastAPI router. (3) IngestRequest.metadata description rewritten to reflect the ADR-021 precedence chain caller > filename parse (only when needs_review=true) > chain inherit (predecessor's doc_type, project, authority_scope when supersedes_document_id is set and the field is omitted) > vault default; the prior chain (manual entry > content extraction > filename extraction > caller-supplied) was inverted relative to ADR-021 and would have misinformed downstream callers. Description-only change; no shape change. ADR-021 implementation Chunks 1-2 of 4.

CAS-ADR-021 cleanup Phase B: vestigial metadata_extraction.review_required removal. The field became read-but-unused once IngestRequest.needs_review (substrate v1.11) became the sole driver of metadata_confirmed at ingest. One change to sage/metadata_extraction.schema.json: removed the review_required property and dropped it from the top-level required array (the schema now has no required properties; an empty metadata_extraction block remains valid). Coordinated removals in code, tests, and live vault configs are tracked in CAS-ADR-021_cleanup.md. No API surface changes; no shape changes elsewhere in the substrate.

Substrate-conformance fix: add the long-missing project_identifier property to sage/metadata_extraction.schema.json under filename_extraction. The field is read by sage/services/filename_parser.py (self._project_id) and used to disambiguate a leading short-uppercase filename segment from a code (matching segment is classified as the document's project rather than as a code, overriding known_code_patterns). It has been present in the example_vault vault YAML and in SAGE/app test fixtures since before CAS-ADR-021, but was absent from the schema's filename_extraction.additionalProperties=false allowlist, so a strict JSON Schema validation pass against example_vault failed even when the runtime path (Pydantic VaultConfig) accepted it. Discovered during CAS-ADR-021 cleanup Phase B verification and originally flagged as out-of-scope in CAS-ADR-021_cleanup.md; landed as a separate substrate-conformance commit. No code, test, or YAML edits required -- the field is already consumed correctly everywhere it appears. The CAS Application API spec already references project_identifier (cas_app_api.openapi.yaml ParseFilenameResponse.project description).

Additive widening of IngestRequest.metadata to support list-typed values for the tags field, plus a paired implementation fix. One change to sage/sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: metadata.additionalProperties widened from `type: string` to `oneOf: [string, array<string>]`. Backward compatible (every prior shape still validates). Motivated by a defect: ingest_document's docstring promised that a comma-separated tags string would land on doc.tags, but sage/services/ingestion.py:_build_metadata_updates lacked a `tags` branch and silently dropped the value, requiring callers to ingest first then call update_metadata to apply tags. The implementation fix adds the missing branch (accepts list[str] OR comma-separated string); the schema widening allows the list form -- which update_metadata already accepts -- to flow through ingest as well, removing the cross-tool shape mismatch. No new architectural constraint; no ADR required. Ingestion regression coverage added at tests/sage/test_ad021_ingestion.py (TEST-AD021-010 through 014).

Tier 3 typed per-doc_type metadata via tier3_metadata, Phase 1 plumbing. One schema change to sage/document_types.schema.json: each DocTypeEntry may now declare an optional metadata_schema (JSON Schema draft 2020-12 fragment) validating the structure of tier3_metadata payloads at the SAGE API boundary. When metadata_schema is omitted, doc_types reject any tier3_metadata payload with 400 tier3_schema_violation; when present, payloads must validate against the fragment. The Document model already carried a tier3_metadata dict|None field and the SQLite documents table already had a tier3_metadata TEXT JSON column with round-trip serialization wired through graph_store; Phase 1 activates the field by extending IngestRequest, UpdateMetadataRequest, and RetrievalFilters Pydantic models, adding a validator cache on VaultConfig keyed by doc_type, introducing a Tier3SchemaViolationError class, wiring validation into ingestion and metadata services, and extending the retrieval filter pipeline (RetrievalFilters.tier3) to filter both catalog and semantic modes by tier3 subfield equality (None means absent-or-null). MCP tool surface gains tier3_metadata parameters on ingest_document and update_metadata; search already accepts a generic filters dict, so the new tier3 clause flows through without signature change. Phase 1 vault-config rollout declares metadata_schema for the cas vault's failure_record and ticket doc_types only; Phase 2 (deferred to a separate ticket) will migrate existing failure_records and tickets into tier3_metadata, strip the now-redundant tag prefixes, revise the two governing steering documents, write the Tier 2 vs Tier 3 distinction ADR, and rewrite the cas-ticket-management skill to use tier3-based queries.

Tier 3 typed metadata Phase 2 rollout. No schema or API shape changes; this entry records the data-migration and governance milestone. Migration script scripts/migrate_tier3_metadata.py backfilled tier3_metadata on all 63 existing cas-vault tickets and failure_records (14 failure_record versions + 49 ticket versions across supersedes chains), parsing values from the tag grammar and (for failure_records) the body `## Metadata` header, then stripping the migrated tag prefixes (`id:T-*`, `type:*`, `priority:*` on tickets; `id:F*`, `class:*`, `severity:*`, `observed_by:*` on failure_records). Body `## Metadata` headers are retained as historical commentary. The CAS Ticket Conventions (head 8f529885_cas_ticket_conventions) and CAS Failure Record Conventions (head 15077926_cas_failure_record_conventions) steering documents were superseded with revised bodies that declare tier3_metadata authoritative for the structured fields and present worked search examples with filters={"tier3": {...}}. ADR-028 (Tier-2 doc_type vocabulary and Tier-3 typed metadata as orthogonal vault-config facets) was added to the vault with references edges to ADR-021, ADR-024, the two revised steering documents,, and. The cas-ticket-management Claude Code skill was rewritten (v0.4.0) to use tier3 filters in every query path including the hygiene-scan collision detection. The cas-code-review skill does not yet exist; when authored, it must consult the revised conventions surface from the start.

update_metadata patch-mode redesign (CAS-ADR-028 revision). Three changes to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) UpdateMetadataRequest.tags switched from `array<string>` (wholesale replacement) to `$ref: TagsPatch` (ops object with `add` / `remove`). (2) UpdateMetadataRequest.tier3_metadata added (previously absent in OpenAPI despite being live in the Pydantic model and service layer; pre-existing schema/Pydantic drift closed as side effect), now `$ref: Tier3Patch` (ops object with `set` / `unset`). (3) New `TagsPatch` and `Tier3Patch` component schemas with strict-conflict semantics: adding a tag already present, removing a tag absent, or unsetting a tier3 key absent each return 400 (`tag_add_conflict` / `tag_remove_conflict` / `tier3_unset_conflict`); `tag_patch_overlap` / `tier3_patch_overlap` for disjoint-list violations; `patch_empty` for degenerate empty ops; `legacy_form` raised at the MCP boundary when callers pass the deprecated bare-list / bare-dict shapes, with a worked-example string in the error detail. Conflict errors carry `current_tags` / `current_tier3_keys` in detail (computed inside the document lock, free). `set` on an existing tier3 key overwrites without error (the verb is literal). The merged tier3 dict is validated against the resolved doc_type's metadata_schema after applying the patch in memory; an individually-valid patch that produces an invalid merged result returns 400 tier3_schema_violation. `ingest_document` is unchanged: it still takes `tags` as a list and `tier3_metadata` as a dict (creation supplies complete state). The asymmetry mirrors REST POST vs PATCH idiom and eliminates the read-modify-write ceremony on single-field edits in the cas-ticket-management skill's Workflow 2 and any future skill touching Tier-3-bearing doc_types. Hard break: bare-list / bare-dict forms on `update_metadata` are rejected (`legacy_form` 400); the skill, the CAS Ticket Conventions steering doc, the CAS Failure Record Conventions steering doc, and ADR-028 are revised in lockstep. Pydantic gains `TagsPatch` and `Tier3Patch` models with `model_config={'extra': 'forbid'}` and `model_validator(mode='after')` enforcing the disjoint/non-empty/non-duplicate invariants; `UpdateMetadataRequest` also gains `extra='forbid'` to catch field-name typos. Service layer (`MetadataService.update_metadata`) reads current state inside the existing document lock, applies the patch in memory, validates the merged tier3 against the doc_type's schema, then writes the final field values to the graph store (no storage-layer change; the JSON TEXT columns continue to accept final-value dicts). Coverage at tests/sage/test_request_validators.py (18 new tests on the Pydantic validators), tests/sage/test_tier3_metadata.py (8 rewrites + new patch happy-path / unset-conflict / post-merge / set-overwrite / unset-only coverage), and tests/sage/test_mcp_server.py (8 new tests covering tag-add / tag-remove / combined / conflict envelopes / legacy-form rejection).

Typed rationale-kind discriminator on edges (CAS-ADR-019 follow-through). Three additions to sage_core_api.openapi.yaml: (1) New `RationaleKind` component schema, string enum over {version_chain, references_mention, filename_code_match, manual} with default `manual`. (2) `Edge.rationale_kind` field referencing the new schema; typed discriminator for the provenance source of the rationale text, promoted from the rationale-prefix string convention (CAS-ADR-019) to a typed, indexed column (idx_edges_rationale_kind) on the edges table so chain-repair and future inference rules filter via SQL rather than Python startswith() (F-9). (3) `LinkRequest.rationale_kind` optional field; when omitted, the service derives the value from the rationale text prefix and falls back to `manual`. Identifier-mention edge inference. One change to sage/edge_inference.schema.json (bumped to v0.2): adds `identifier_mention` to the inference-method enum and introduces a structured `patterns` array on inference rules, where each pattern object carries a `regex`, a `target_tags` filter (with `{id}` placeholder for the matched literal), an optional `target_title_prefix` (also with `{id}` placeholder for ADR-style identifiers whose tag is generic but title carries the id prefix), an optional `target_doc_type`, and an optional `enabled` flag. The `content_reference` method remains in the enum as a placeholder; the cas vault config is migrated to `identifier_mention` and promoted from Tier 2 to Tier 1 with three default patterns (CAS-ADR-NNN via `adr` tag plus title-prefix match, T-NNNN via `id:{id}` tag, F-N via `id:{id}` tag). The corresponding rationale-kind discriminator (`references_mention`) and prefix were pre-staged in substrate v1.19; this entry activates them by landing the inference rule that emits them. No API surface change.

Abstraction provider/model relocated from per-vault to SAGE-stack scope (CAS-ADR-030). Two substrate changes: (1) new schema sage/sage_core_config.schema.json (v0.1) defines a stack-wide `abstraction:` block carrying `provider` (Literal enum `qwen3-mlx`/`stub`, default `qwen3-mlx`) and `model` (`string | null`, default null). The on-disk file is sage/config.yaml at the repo root, loaded once at SAGE process startup before any vault is registered. (2) sage/vault_config.schema.json bumped to v0.3: the `abstraction` block drops the `provider` and `model` properties (formerly per-vault), keeping only `enabled` and the density-proportional token-budget fields (`max_abstract_tokens`, `base_abstract_tokens`, `tokens_per_word`). The block description is rewritten to reflect the new scope split. Vault YAMLs that retained `model` or `provider` fail loud at startup against the stricter (still `additionalProperties: false`) block. Pydantic `AbstractionConfig` in sage/config.py splits into `VaultAbstractionConfig` (vault scope) and `StackAbstractionConfig` (stack scope), both derived from their respective JSON schemas per Principle 8. The factory dispatch in sage/mcp_init.py moves to a stack-startup helper `build_stack_abstraction_provider`; per-vault `initialize_services` consults only the `enabled` opt-out and accepts the stack provider via injection. `SAGE_TEST_STUB_PROVIDERS=1` short-circuits at stack startup, preserving the/F-8 guardrail. Test surface: DI-008..DI-012 in tests/sage/test_mcp_init.py absorb into new stack-scope tests (STK-001..005 in tests/sage/test_stack_abstraction_dispatch.py); per-vault DI-008/DI-009 are rewritten as the `enabled=False` opt-out anti-coincidence pair; new schema-validation tests cover the stack-scope schema (SCH-S-001..004 in tests/sage/test_sage_core_config_schema.py); vault SCH-001 is rewritten to assert `provider` and `model` are NOT in the vault schema. The verbatim-description sync test gains a new (StackAbstractionConfig, sage_core_config.schema.json) entry. `get_vault_config` MCP response naturally drops `abstraction.{provider,model}` via the Pydantic model split; the complementary new MCP tool `get_stack_config` exposes the stack-wide abstraction config.

Vault-config-declared tier3 uniqueness enforcement (CAS-ADR-031). One schema change to sage/document_types.schema.json (bumped to v0.3): each DocTypeEntry may now declare an optional unique_keys list naming tier3_metadata fields whose values must be unique within the doc_type across all lifecycle statuses. A doc_type with no unique_keys (or an empty list) preserves current behavior. The substrate enforces uniqueness atomically via partial UNIQUE expression indexes on json_extract(tier3_metadata, '$.<field>') scoped per (doc_type, field), with WHERE lifecycle_status != 'superseded' so the supersession-chain exception (CAS-ADR-031 §3) drops out of the partial filter; the supersession-insert path in graph_store.py is reordered to mark the predecessor superseded before inserting the successor. New Tier3UniqueConstraintViolation (409, error_code 'tier3_unique_constraint_violation') in sage/api/errors.py with doc_type / field / colliding_value / existing_document_id in the structured detail. Pydantic DocTypeEntry in sage/config.py gains unique_keys: list[str] | None and a cross-field validator (each entry must name a metadata_schema property). MaintenanceService grows scan_tier3_uniqueness_collisions and the migration tool refuses to activate the constraint while collisions exist (CAS-ADR-031 §5); collisions are surfaced via the MigrationReport. The cas-ticket-management skill's W1.1 allocator gains a 409-retry branch and the steering doc retracts its 'out of scope for SAGE' caveat. No vault_config.yaml opt-ins land in this revision; activation per doc_type is operator follow-on.

identifier_mention resolver targets via tier3_metadata. One additive schema change to sage/edge_inference.schema.json (bumped to v0.3): the pattern object for the identifier_mention method gains an optional target_tier3 field — an object mapping tier3_metadata keys to exact-match values (strings may carry the `{id}` placeholder for the matched identifier literal). The pattern's `required` list relaxes from `[regex, target_tags]` to `[regex]`, paired with an `anyOf` constraint requiring at least one of `target_tags` or `target_tier3` so a pattern cannot omit both resolver hints. Existing patterns that declare target_tags continue to validate unchanged; the cas vault's CAS-ADR-NNN and F-N patterns are untouched. Motivation: ticket identity is canonicalized in tier3_metadata.ticket_id under CAS-ADR-028, not in tags, so the prior target_tags=['id:{id}'] pattern matched zero tickets after an earlier migration stripped the id:T-NNNN prefixes. Surfaced by a post-restart ingest. Resolver in sage/services/identifier_mention_inference.py threads the new key through `_resolve_identifier` by populating `filters["tier3"]` with the substituted dict, reusing `_format_tag` for the placeholder substitution; the storage-layer tier3 filter (substrate v1.15) carries the equality semantics. Coverage at tests/app/test_edge_inference_identifier_mention.py: test_t2_* and test_t2_sage_ingest_* are rewritten to seed tickets via a tier3_metadata ticket_id with a decoy ticket that ensures the test fails if the resolver falls back to a doc_type-only lookup; new test_t2b (decoy discrimination) and test_t2c (unresolved + decoy) load-bear the anti-coincidence guarantee; new test_pattern_schema_* trio validates the schema's anyOf constraint accepts target_tier3-only, accepts target_tags-only, and rejects neither-target. cas vault config (~/sage_vaults/cas/vault_config.yaml) is updated in lockstep to use target_tier3 for the T-NNNN pattern.

Synced-from provenance attributes on edges, schema-only. Two new nullable TEXT columns on the edges table: synced_from_version (the source-chain version a copy or derivation was taken from at edge assertion) and synced_from_content_hash (the source document's source_content_hash at edge assertion, as an optional companion that survives version-label reuse). Both promote the synced-from fact from free-text rationale prose to a structured, queryable edge attribute, unblocking later drift detection without further migration. Surface changes: paired additions to the Pydantic Edge and LinkRequest models in sage/models/schemas.py and the Edge / LinkRequest schemas in sage/sage_core_api.openapi.yaml (descriptions verbatim-synced); MIGRATION_PLAN entries plus matching EDGES_TABLE CREATE additions so cold-start and existing databases both gain the columns; create_edge MCP tool grows two optional kwargs; service-layer threading in GraphOpsService._link_impl is pass-through (no derivation logic). Semantically meaningful only on sync_target (Tier 1, populated automatically once the deferred Tier-1 inference subsystem ships per) and derived_from (Tier 3, agent-supplied via create_edge today); other edge types may receive values but the substrate adds no write-time edge-type restriction in v1. Field descriptions explicitly distinguish the new attributes from source_valid_from_version / target_valid_from_version (CAS-ADR-017 chain visibility); unset means explicit null and is never inferred from chain anchors. Deferred to follow-up tickets, each tagged follow-up with a depends_on edge to the originating change: (drift-detection tool + conservative rationale-prose backfill + index on synced_from_content_hash + write-time edge-type restriction), (Tier-1 sync_target auto-population at re-ingestion); example-verbatim-sync skill update is out-of-repo and lands after the prior detection tool exists. Per-vault rollout (cas, example_vault, editorial) is caller-driven per CAS-ADR-029 via migrate_vault. Tests at tests/sage/test_synced_from_provenance.py (TEST-1 round-trip via create_edge → traverse, TEST-2 omitted defaults to None and stores SQL NULL via direct SELECT read-back, TEST-3 one-set one-null boundary, TEST-5 Pydantic type rejection at the router boundary) and tests/sage/test_migrate_flag.py (TEST-4 migration idempotency on a earlier database). The OpenAPI conformance suite (test_openapi_conformance.py) passes without allowlist additions; verbatim description-sync between Pydantic and YAML is preserved.

Drift-detection tool + write-time guards + backfill + index on the prior synced-from provenance. Six co-shipped changes: (1) New maintenance endpoint POST /sage_vaults/{vault_id}/admin/detect-drift returning DriftReport. Replaces the manual hand-walk phase of the verbatim-sync and terminology-remediation workflows. Per-edge entry carries edge_id, edge_type, source_id, target_id, recorded_version_id / recorded_version_label / recorded_content_hash, current_head_id / current_head_version_label / current_head_content_hash, competing_head_count, and staleness_basis (StalenessBasis enum: content_drift, chain_advanced_no_content_change, recorded_null, chain_nonlinear). Hash is authoritative for the stale/current decision; version doc-id is a display key. Edges whose recorded state matches the head are absent from the report. Three-layer pattern (MaintenanceService.detect_drift -> FastAPI router -> verify_vault_drift MCP wrapper) mirrors the prior migrate_vault and sage_admin_reabstract_deferred precedents. (2) Write-time guard on _link_impl rejects synced_from_* on edge types other than sync_target / derived_from (400 synced_from_inapplicable_edge_type). Fires before any DB read via _validate_link_request_shape. (3) Write-time chain-membership check on _link_impl: when synced_from_version is set on a sync_target / derived_from edge, the value must be a member of target_id's supersedes chain. Otherwise 400 synced_from_version_not_in_source_chain (NOT document_not_found, so operators can distinguish wrong-document from missing-document). Runs under link_lock so the chain read serializes with the edge insert. (4) synced_from_content_hash retyped from str|None to Sha256Str|None on the Edge and LinkRequest Pydantic models; FastMCP create_edge tool wraps the param in _SHA256_ADAPTER.validate_python. Pydantic 422 envelope on malformed hash. Clears the three KNOWN_VIOLATIONS entries left pinned in tests/sage/test_typed_alias_coverage.py. (5) Conservative rationale-prose backfill (Backfill name=synced_from_version_from_rationale appended to BACKFILL_PLAN). Verb-gated regex (derived|synced|copied|adapted|based + from|on + v?N.N(.N)?) recovers synced_from_version on legacy derived_from edges whose rationale unambiguously names exactly one chain entry's version_label. Ambiguous matches stay NULL by design; false provenance is worse than honest null. (6) New POST_MIGRATION_DDL entry idx_edges_synced_from_content_hash supporting the detector's hash-comparison scan; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN verified. Tests at tests/sage/test_maintenance_service.py (T-DD-multi, T-DD-nonlinear, T-DD-version-only), tests/sage/test_sage_admin_detect_drift.py (MCP wrapper round-trip + error envelopes), tests/sage/test_graph_ops.py (inapplicable-edge-type + chain-membership rejection / acceptance), tests/sage/test_request_validators.py (Sha256Str retype on LinkRequest.synced_from_content_hash), tests/sage/test_t0111_synced_from_backfill.py (T-BF-happy / ambiguous-and-mixed / verb-gate / idempotent), tests/sage/test_t0074_indexes.py (idx_edges_synced_from_content_hash planner-selection). All anti-coincidental-pass drills passed: each new test fails when its keyed production change is reverted. The example-verbatim-sync skill (out-of-repo) will be updated separately to call the new MCP tool.
